title: Winnie the Pooh: Silly Old Bear
summary: On Dec 24, 1925, the world got a Christmas gift from a little-known writer named A.A. Milne when the first Winnie the Pooh story was published. Milne was inspired by the imaginative woodland strolls he shared with his son, the real-life Christopher Robin.

title: Selects: Sacagawea: Impressive Teen
summary: Sacagawea was only 16 when she joined the Corps of Discovery. That is one seriously impressive teenager. Find out all about her in this classic episode.

title: The Disappearance of Dorothy Arnold
summary: When socialite Dorothy Arnold disappeared in 1910, no one imagined the case would remain forever unsolved. Today we tell her story.

title: Short Stuff: Currency Symbols
summary: In today's shorty, Josh and Chuck go over the stories behind some of the world's currency symbols.

title: Asteroooooid De-FENSE!
summary: There’s no question that millions of asteroids are circling the Earth at incredible speed and every one of them is just dying to get a chance to smoosh our planet and wipe out life in the universe once and for all. But Earth has an ace up its sleeve: Us!

title: Selects: What's the deal with swing states?
summary: Swing states are all the rage once again this election season, but the makeup has changed a bit. In this classic episode, learn all about what makes a swing state a swing state right now.

title: Stand-Up Pt II
summary: The SYSK boys continue the episode on stand-up comedy in part two, placing it in the rarefied company of other two-parters like Evel Knievel, the Hoover Dam, and the Trail of Tears. In this ep: should anything be off limits for stand-up? Consensus: no.

title: Short Stuff: The Style Cycle
summary: Why do clothing styles get stale and then come back into fashion? Listen in to find out.

title: Stand-Up Comedy Pt I
summary: Chuck and Josh do their best to tackle “the craft,” which most normal people call stand-up comedy. Stand-up dates back to the vaudeville days but it really started to take off in the 60s when comics stopped wearing suits and started getting edgy.

title: Selects: How Bras Work
summary: Bras are loved and hated, sometimes at the same time. But as difficult and restrictive as they can be, they rescued women from a much cruel contraption: corsets. The question remains, though, do women need bras at all? Listen to this classic episode to find out.

title: Let's Thank Universal Pictures for Monster Movies!
summary: Basically everything you think of when you think of vampires, mummies, werewolves, and Frankenstein all come from a spate of films made in the 1930s, and every one of them by Universal Pictures. Amazingly, they are still among the best films ever made.

title: Short Stuff: The Retirement Curse
summary: Is retirement bad for your health? Well it certainly can be if you don't take steps to prevent it. Listen in to learn more about the "retirement curse."

title: A Good Walk Ruined: The History of Golf
summary: The history of golf is a bit muddled, but once it was truly born in Scotland, it started the beginning of lifelong obsessions for people dumb enough to pick up a club and give it a try. Learn all about the early history of the most frustrating game ever invented.

title: Selects: Wetlands! Wetlands! Wetlands!
summary: It’s time to get jazzed up for some Earth science of the waterlogged variety. Join Chuck and Josh in this classic episode as they tour some of the most interesting ecosystems on the planet and learn why we need to stop destroying them post haste.

title: Introducing 3 Putt Bogey
summary: 3 Putt Bogey is a golf podcast hosted by Chuck Bryant and Adam Pranica, two mid handicappers who are just good enough to know exactly how bad they still are. The name says it all: one great shot, followed immediately by the kind of self-inflicted disaster only a mid-handicap golfer can produce. That's the whole sport, really, and this show lives in that gap. Every week, Chuck and Adam break down their most recent rounds, dig through the bag, and try to actually get better — which is harder than it sounds when social media serves up an endless, contradictory firehose of tips, drills, and gear you're told you absolutely need. They'll talk about what's actually working, what's total crap, and what happened when they tried it on the course anyway. Expect gear talk, course recaps, golf movies and video games, rules debates, questionable gambling picks, and a healthy amount of self-inflicted misery, all in service of two guys trying to shave a few strokes off their game and laugh about it along the way.

title: Emily Post: Ettiquette Queen
summary: In today's episode, we detail the life and times of ettiquette queen Emily Post.

title: Short Stuff: Mabon
summary: Mabon is often called the Pagan Thanksgiving but though it seems like it’s as ancient as Halloween, it’s actually only around 50 years old. But, pagan or not, it’s a great chance to really feel the fall and thank Mother Earth.

title: Our Big Fat Dream Episode
summary: No you’re no dreaming – go ahead, pinch yourself – we’ve finally made an episode on dreams! We’ve done episodes on lucid dreaming, night terrors, sleepwalking, sleep paralysis – basically everything but dreams themselves. Well, at long last here it is!

title: Selects: Fallout Shelters: Probably Useless (Let’s Never Find Out)
summary: The advent of nuclear weapons and the Cold War kicked off a craze in the US for building rec rooms with foot-thick reinforced walls and outfitted with survival rations and board games. Would they work? Probably not. Find out (but not really) in this classic episode.

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: What is Collective Hysteria?
summary: Throughout the history of the world, there have been many cases of what is known as collective hysteria - groups of people, usually young women, who all exhibit the same physical symptoms of non-existent conditions. Is it psychosomatic? Is it group think?

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: What was the Philadelphia Experiment?
summary: The Philadelphia Experiment is a bad movie from the 1980s, and also the conspiracy theory that refuses to die, despite virtually zero evidence of its occurrence. Learn all about this strange non-event in today's show.

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: Mermaids: Not a real thing
summary: Mermaids aren't real. That much we know. But the history and lore of these magical and sometimes menacing creatures of the sea is pretty interesting stuff. Learn all about these half women/half fish today.

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: Will We Find Evidence of Aliens by Their Engineering Projects?
summary: In 1960 physicist Freeman Dyson suggested that in the hunt for alien life, we should search for evidence of massive engineering projects that encapsulate stars with solar arrays to harness their energy. Could we humans ever make one ourselves?

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: The Mystery of the Mary Celeste
summary: When the Mary Celeste was discovered floating and abandoned in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean one day in 1872, the legend of the ghost ship was born. Why did the Mary Celeste’s crew disappear? Was it pirates? Mutiny? UFOs? Well, probably not that last one.

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: The Max Headroom Incident
summary: In 1987, a very strange broadcast intrusion occurred in the city of Chicago. For just a couple of minutes, the odd TV character Max Headroom appeared onscreen in the middle of an episode of Dr. Who. He spoke in garbled tones, brandished a marital aid, and was spanked on the rear with a fly swatter by a person dressed in Annie Oakley garb. If this sounds weird, it is. It's the Max Headroom Incident.

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: Dragons: As Real as Mermaids
summary: Dragons are like mermaids in that they're not real. And that's about where the comparison ends. Learn all about dragons today.

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: The Creepy Legacy of the Hotel Cecil
summary: The Hotel Cecil in downtown Los Angeles has had no less than 16 unnatural deaths, from suicides to murders and everything in between. Listen in to the history of this decidedly creepy hotel.

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: What's the deal with blue people?
summary: The famous blue people of Kentucky are no longer blue. But why were they like that in the first place?

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: Doppelgängers: Hey you, you're me!
summary: Seeing your near twin is probably pretty weird. But could there be a genetic commonality as well? You bet there could!

title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: The Story of the Nuclear Boy Scout
summary: David Hahn was a kid who was really into science. So much that he built a nuclear reactor in his mother's potting shed. And it worked.

title: The Cancer Episode
summary: Cancer is a terrible word in any language for at least two reasons: It’s incredibly difficult to get rid of once it grows in the body, and there’s a very good chance that you or someone close to you will be diagnosed with it. But hope is growing.

title: Short Stuff: Leisure Suits
summary: You know the leisure suit, perhaps the tackiest suit to ever be invented. It was so huge in the 70s and spread as wide the lapels of the shirts worn with them. Then, as fast as they hit the scene they disappeared in shame.

title: How Boredom Works
summary: Are there benefits to boredom? Or is it all negative? Why do we get bored? What can we do to break free from boredom? The answers to those questions and more are coming your way today.

title: Selects: Wasps: Not as cute as bees
summary: Wasps have a bad rap. Because their sting really hurts and they don't make honey like their cousins. But they are super cool and you shouldn't kill them. Listen to this classic episode and learn!

title: The Odyssey Episode
summary: Why does the story of The Odyssey endure this many years after it was first spoken? Listen in to find out.

title: Short Stuff: Flappers
summary: In the 1920s, a certain set of women wanted to loosen up and have a good time. Today, we get into it with the flappers.

title: Nickelodeon:The Best of Slimes
summary: Today we tell the story of the kids TV network that changed it all, Nickelodeon.

title: Selects: Blacksmiths? You got that right!
summary: Blacksmiths? You got that right. Learn all about this age old occupation in this classic episode.

title: Social Identity Theory: Your Group Rules, Others Drool
summary: In the 80s, a pair of psychologists theorized why being part of a group can change people’s thoughts and feelings, both about themselves and other people. It sounds dry, but SIT explains everything from how people justify genocide to football rivalries.

title: Short Stuff: Hisashi Ouchi
summary: Japanese nuclear worker Hisashi Ouchi is often called on the internet “the world’s most radioactive man.” That’s not exactly true, but it gets the point across about how severe the fatal dose of radiation he received was.

title: Terry Fox: Greatest Canadian Hero
summary: It is to the great nation of Canada’s lasting credit that it has prized Terry Fox as one of the most beloved and admired citizens for nearly 50 years now. It’s difficult to get across how much he means to Canada. Lucky for us, his story speaks for itself.

title: Selects: Flagpole Sitting: A Real Fad
summary: The 1920s were just absolutely nuts. People got into weird fads really intensely and one of the strangest of all was flagpole sitting. It’s just what it sounds like – sitting on top of a flagpole for as long as you can. One man sat above them all. Learn all about him and many of these wild fads in this classic episode.

title: The Fall of the USSR, Pt II
summary: The break-up of the USSR was a tough one for Russia, being the jilted republic. For the entire decade after, the country plunged into a type of controlled chaos, with a rampantly corrupt kleptocracy taking the place of the toppled socialist society.

title: SYSK Tribute: Why does everyone love Dolly Parton?
summary: Today we dive in to celebrate the international treasure that is Dolly Parton. Why is she nearly universally loved? Listen in to find out.

title: Short Stuff: Cyclospora
summary: The US has an unusual number of outbreaks of food-borne illness going on in the summer of 2026, and the star of the show is cyclospora. How does this parasite make people sick, where does it come from? You may not want to know.

title: The Fall of the USSR, Pt I
summary: It’s rare that the downfall of an empire can be chalked up to the decisions of just one person. It’s even rarer, when the empire falls over the course of a year. That’s pretty much what happened with the Soviet Union when Mikhail Gorbachev dissolved it.

title: Selects: How Narcolepsy Works
summary: Narcolepsy is one of those amazing rare disorders that everyone thinks they understand – people just fall asleep at random times, even in the middle of doing something. But there’s a lot more to it and – even better – we actually may be able to explain it. Josh and Chuck run it down in this classic episode.

title: Rope, yeah ROPE!
summary: Rope is one of the unsung heroes of the world of inventions. Think about it. Then let us tell you about it.

title: Short Stuff: Did a shipwreck double the size of the United States?
summary: Did a shipwreck double the size of the United States? Sort of. Listen in to find out what the heck that means.

title: Isn't It Ironic, Dontcha Think?
summary: Irony is one of those things that you know when you see it, but it’s almost impossible to define. Well, that’s not quite right – there are a ton of definitions for irony but none of them quite capture it fully. Want to know what irony is? So do we!

title: Selects: The Manhattan Grid
summary: Ever wanted to know more about how the Manhattan grid was made? Well this is your chance. Find out all about it in this classic episode.

title: Who was Robert Maxwell?
summary: Robert Maxwell was a lot of things, publisher, mogul, spy, politician, crook. But was he murdered when he fell from his yacht?

title: Short Stuff: Nero and His Fiddle
summary: Did Nero play his fiddle while Rome burned during the Great Fire of 64 CE? Absolutely not. Find out how we know when Chuck and Josh bust a two thousand year-old myth.

title: Bonnie and Clyde
summary: You've probably seen the movie, but what else do you know about this legendary crime couple? Listen in to find out.

title: Selects: Iran-Contra Affair: Shady in the 80s, Part 2
summary: As the operation expands it also begins to unravel. Word starts to leak out of the illegal stuff the Reagan administration was up to, Congress and the press investigate and people start to point fingers. Spoiler alert – they all got off scot free. Find out how it all wraps up in part 2 of this classic story.

title: Selects: Iran-Contra Affair: Shady in the 80s, Part 1
summary: When Ronald Reagan was president, America got involved in some deeply shady stuff, not the least of which was the Iran-Contra scandal – a convoluted operation that managed to combine an illegal covert war in Nicaragua with secretly selling arms to Iran. Learn all about it with Josh and Chuck in this classic episode.

title: Reggae: Kingston’s Gift to the World
summary: Although it was built atop some musical styles that came before, reggae is mostly its own thing. It evolved as local music in the Trenchtown neighborhood in Kingston, Jamaica but after Bob Marley and the Wailers came along, it became a global phenomenon.

title: Short Stuff: Phone Books
summary: Once upon a time there were these things called phone books. Inside you could find the phone number and address of just about everyone in your town. Can you imagine?

title: Beans and Rice Feeds the World
summary: To call beans and rice a staple is to undersell the importance of beans and rice. Today we break down the ubiquity of this beloved food combo.

title: Selects: How Peanut Butter Works
summary: No food is more all-American than peanut butter – 80 percent of homes in the country have a jar of it in the pantry right now. And while the rest of the world might find peanut butter peculiar, maybe even gross, the rest of the world is wrong. Enjoy a smooth ride through one of our top condiments in this classic episode.

title: How Russia Shapes What the World Thinks
summary: Operation Doppelganger was a Russian propaganda project discovered in 2022, a minor part of the enormous, ongoing disinformation and chaos-sewing campaign Russia spreads across the world through social media. And some of your views may have come from it.

title: Short Stuff: Shark Arm Murders
summary: Get yer info on one of Australia’s great true crime cases he-re!

title: The Beloved Judy Blume
summary: Judy Blume is more than an author. She's a legend in teen literature for her frank and honest portrayals of adolescence. Today we pay tribute to her.

title: Selects: Plant Migration
summary: Climate change is having sweeping effects on our climate and this is changing the world, not just for humans and other animals, but plants too. Will the Earth’s flora manage to find safe refuge in time? Josh and Chuck run down the odds in this classic episode.

title: What's the deal with Swiss neutrality?
summary: We all know Switzerland is neutral. But why? Listen in and you might learn something.

title: Short Stuff: Sardines!
summary: Josh implored Chuck to try sardines. Did he? Listen in to find out.

title: The Tobacco Master Settlement: That Time We Got Em
summary: By the 1990s, cigarette makers had been hooking and killing off their customers for about a century. And they’d gotten good at both as well as covering up their harms. In 1994 they were still denying cigarettes were addictive. Then, the 50 Attorneys General of the US rode into town to take them on.

title: Selects: The Soul Train Episode
summary: In this classic episode, Chuck and Josh dive into the funky, cool world of the classic TV show, Sooooooooul Train.

title: White Boy Rick
summary: Would you believe that Detroit’s crack epidemic in the mid-80s was overseen by one 16 year-old white kid who supplied all the coke? No? Well, that’s not quite true, so okay. The actual story is even more nutso than that.

title: Short Stuff: The Voice of God
summary: Today we salute the great Don LaFontaine, aka The Voice of God in movie and TV trailers.

title: You Are Not Alone With Postpartum Depression
summary: Most new moms get the baby blues soon after giving birth. Postpartum depression is something much different - the symptoms are similar, but their intensity can have sweeping effects on mom, baby, and the whole family. Fortunately, it’s highly treatable but the catch is moms usually have to ask for help.

title: Selects: The First Road Trip
summary: Back when cars were a brand new thing, before people even knew they'd stick around, two men and a dog drove from San Francisco to New York. This classic episode has their story.

title: Eleanor Roosevelt: Best First Lady
summary: Eleanor Roosevelt was something else. We can't get into it here, but just wait until you listen to this episode.

title: Short Stuff: Great Britain
summary: Now that it’s been 250 years since America split from England, we figure enough time has passed that we can finally learn the difference between the UK, Great Britain, and the British Isles.

title: Kola: The World’s Deepest Hole
summary: During the Cold War all eyes were on the Space Race between the US and USSR. But there was another, overlooked race too and it went in the opposite direction.

title: Selects: Chopsticks > Forks
summary: In this classic episode, Chuck and Josh sit and converse on the simple, elegant chopstick.

title: Alaska Earthquake of 1964
summary: When a 9.2 quake shoook Alaska in 1964 it was the 2nd largest earthquake ever recorded. This is that story.

title: Short Stuff: Toronto Clown Riot
summary: Those are three words you probably never thought you’d see together. And the true story is just as interesting as it sounds.

title: The Hillsborough Disaster
summary: When a crush of football fans killed 97 people in England in 1989, police and officials engaged in a massive cover-up to blame it on drunken fans. Today we tell that story.

title: Selects: How Enron Fooled the World
summary: Until 2007, the largest single corporate bankruptcy was Enron, a $67 billion energy trading company. Its decline was breathtaking, and while it’s a fascinating story of corporate malfeasance and greed, it’s also about the lives of ruined workers. Learn all about it in this classic episode.

title: Freetown Christiania
summary: The sort of commune of Freetown Christiania in Denmark may not be what it used to be, but it's still true to many of its original values. Learn all about this unique neighborhood today.

title: Short Stuff: Why does it feel good to be scared?
summary: Fear is different than being scared, most notably because fear is generally a negative thing and being scared can cause an enjoyable thrill. We'll get into the difference in today's episode.

title: Some Interesting Curses
summary: Even though curses aren’t real – and we go to great pains to make that clear – they are pretty interesting, especially ones you haven’t heard of before. So we dug deep and found some of the curses that don’t always hog the spotlight for this fun episode.

title: Selects: Birthmarks: Probably Not the Mark of the Devil
summary: It’s a pretty safe assumption that people have been born with birthmarks since humanity began, and between then and now we’ve come up with some wacky, even dangerous, explanations for them – even a few that survive still today. Learn all about them in this classic episode.

title: The Stuff You Should Know Doin’ Science Playlist: How Chaos Theory Changed the Universe
summary: Since the age of Descartes, science has put all of its eggs in the basket of determinism, the idea that with accurate enough measurements any aspect of the universe could be predicted. But the universe, it turns out, is not so tidy.

title: The Stuff You Should Know Doin’ Science Playlist: How Global Warming Works
summary: It's a confusing part of climate change when it seems winter is as cold as ever, but as global temperatures creep ever so slightly higher, a cascade of catastrophic events will almost surely follow. The ball is in humanity's court.

title: The Stuff You Should Know Doin’ Science Playlist: How X-Rays Work
summary: Like many huge discoveries, X-rays were accidentally stumbled upon. That serendipity led to a medical breakthrough still in use today. Learn about how X-rays are created and why they make such delightful images of our bones.

title: The Stuff You Should Know Doin’ Science Playlist: Elastics: Where God and Science Smooch
summary: You could be forgiven for thinking the story behind elastics was boring. You’d still be wrong, though. The story of what’s holding up your underwear is a global drama, replete with war, industrial espionage, colonialism, destitute inventors – everything!

title: The Stuff You Should Know Doin’ Science Playlist: Can Nuclear Fusion Reactors Save The World?
summary: The world's energy consumption is ruining the planet but for decades physicists have been working on what could solve the world's energy and climate change woes for centuries to come - nuclear fusion. Learn about building stars on Earth in this episode.

title: The Stuff You Should Know Doin’ Science Playlist: How Occam's Razor Works
summary: You know the rule that says the simplest explanation is probably the correct one? That’s called a razor and it’s meant to guide logic. But over time it’s become a broadsword used to disprove opposing arguments. Learn how to spot a faux skeptic in this episode.

title: The Stuff You Should Know Doin’ Science Playlist: Things We Believed Before the Scientific Method
summary: It’s easy to think of people in the distant past as kinda dumb for believing things like that mice could spontaneously generate from old grain. But if you look a little deeper, you’ll find there was a sensibility to the odd beliefs that came before science.

title: The Stuff You Should Know Doin’ Science Playlist: How Big Bang Theory Works, with Neil deGrasse Tyson
summary: There are a number of theories for how the universe evolved but none are more widely accepted than the Big Bang theory. Learn about the mind-boggling details of the early universe and hear Dr. Neil deGrasse Tyson talk about what it will take for us to know its origins.

title: The Stuff You Should Know Doin’ Science Playlist: How the Scientific Method Works
summary: It evolved over centuries to become the gold standard for conducting scientific inquiry. Yet many people - including some scientists - don't fully understand it. Learn about the basis of how we explore our world in this episode.

title: The Stuff You Should Know Doin’ Science Playlist: Legs! Legs! Legs! (The Periodic Table)
summary: If you’ve ever wanted to listen to two totally untrained, non-chemists who are fully unqualified to explain how the periodic table works nervously explain how the periodic table works, then this episode is for you. Chemistry majors, be warned.

title: M*A*S*H: The Story of the 4077th
summary: Chuck loved M*A*S*H. Josh didn't. Listen in as they fight to the death.

title: Short Stuff: Does singing make you happy?
summary: Does singing make you happy? Yes, yes it does.

title: Did 24-Hour Cable News Kill America?
summary: You can make a pretty good case that the rise of opinion “news” and filter bubbles on cable tv created the current cultural and political schism that plagues American society. How did it start? Where did it come from? And what the heck can we do about it?

title: Selects: How the Fairness Doctrine Worked
summary: Back in the day, broadcasters were bound by law to provide contrasting opinions on political matters. Why? Because of the Fairness Doctrine. What happened to it? Listen to this classic episode and find out.

title: The NY Subway Vigilante
summary: Today we dive into the unremorseful life of NYC Subway vigilante Bernhard Goetz.

title: Short Stuff: Rain Barrels!
summary: Harvesting rainwater has tons of upsides and not many downsides – you just need to take a few precautions first. Don’t miss this episode, which features some Josh Math™.

title: Smile
summary: They say that smiling requires fewer muscles than frowning, so why not smile? That doesn’t seem to be true, or at least unproven, and there is lots more about smiling that will keep you glued to your earbuds in this fun episode.

title: Selects: 911 Is Not a Joke
summary: Josh and Chuck delve into the world of 911 in this classic episode.

title: Three Mile Island
summary: The disaster at Three Mile Island thankfully did not cost any lives directly, but the notion that it didn't harm people is very much up in the air. Learn all about the worst nuclear disaster in the history of the United States today.

title: Short Stuff: 1955 Le Mans Disaster
summary: In 1955, the 24 Hours of Le Mans endurance motor race took a very dark turn when a terrible accident on the track continued into the crowd.

title: The Tragic Life of Vincent Van Gogh
summary: Van Gogh lived a troubled life and did not garner attention as a painter until after his death by suicide. Today we dive into this complicated journey as an artist.

title: Selects: Did Shakespeare really write all that stuff?
summary: The question of Shakespeare's authorship has been around since at least the mid-1800s. Is there anything to it? In this classic episode, we dig in to this dense topic to find out.

title: Howard Hughes in Las Vegas
summary: From 1968 to 1972 Howard Hughes holed up in a suite in the Desert Inn casino in Las Vegas. Addicted to morphine and living on candy bars and milk, he was in bad shape. When he was told to leave, he bought the hotel and stayed. Soon he owned half of Vegas.

title: Short Stuff: Knuckle Cracking
summary: Does knuckle cracking give you arthritis? It doesn't appear to. But that doesn't mean it's harmless.

title: The Story of Starvation Heights
summary: There are quacks and then there is Linda Hazzard. Not only did she starve her patients to death, but she took their family fortunes as she did it. This is the story of Starvation Heights.

title: Selects: How Flight Attendants Work
summary: Flight attendants have come a long way. From having to put up with rampant sexism, to the current incarnation as your first line of defense in case of an incident, they are valued airline employees. Learn all about this cool job in this classic episode.

title: The 1993 Waco Siege
summary: One of the darkest days in the history of American law enforcement came on April 19, 1993, when the FBI’s 51-day siege of the Branch Davidian religious sect’s compound in Waco, Texas ended with a fire and 75 men, women, and children dead inside.

title: Short Stuff: All about BPAs
summary: Are BPAs safe? Of course not. Does the FDA care? Of course not. Learn all about what and why today.

title: Eels Alive!
summary: Eels are pretty much objectively unsettling. They’re not quite fish (although they are) and if they’re snakes, they’re messed up snakes (they aren’t). But they’re fascinating too! There are even little cute eels. It’s time you got acquainted with eels!

title: Selects: Did Mallory Make it to the Top of Everest First?
summary: George Mallory was a member of the first three European expeditions to Everest, world’s tallest mountain. He wanted to summit it so badly, he gave his life trying. Since that fateful day in 1924, climbers have wondered – was Mallory the first to summit? Listen as Josh and Chuck explore that question and lots more in this classic episode.

title: The Hindenburg Disaster
summary: Hard to believe we haven't covered this one yet, but here we are. Why did the Hindenburg crash and burn? We still don't really know.

title: Short Stuff: Did Tippi Hedron start the Vietnamese manicure industry?
summary: Strange but true, actor Tippi Hedron kickstsarted the Vietnamese manicure industry in the United States in the 1970s. This is that story.

title: Humanists, the Happy Heathens
summary: If you don’t believe in any kind of god or afterlife - or even that there’s a meaning to life – does that mean you’re doomed to a life of gloom and doom? Heck no!, say humanists. Their philosophical movement says you can make your own meaningful life.

title: Selects: Can movies be cursed?
summary: First of all, movies can't be cursed because curses aren't real. However, that can't stop Josh and Chuck from taking a look at some movies throughout history that have had a disturbing number of bad things surrounding their production and release. Dive into the world of cursed movies in this very fun classic episode.

title: Let's Go to Camp... David!
summary: Camp David is awesome. But not all presidents have liked it. We'll dig into this historic property in today's episiode.

title: Short Stuff: Why do kangaroos hop?
summary: Kangaroos are the only marsupial to hop, which is pretty weird. We'll investigate why.

title: Boeing's Nosedive: The 737-MAX
summary: Boeing used to be one of the most respected engineering firms in the world. Then it changed its focus from making great airplanes to increasing its stock value. The result was the 737-MAX, a plane that took the lives of 346 people in two avoidable crashes.

title: Selects: Thrill to the Stunning Bicameral Mind Hypothesis
summary: Psychologist Julian Jaynes came up with a stunning hypothesis in 1976, that human consciousness only developed in the last 3000 years. And he seemed to have proof in ancient texts. Scholars have been picking it apart ever since and in this classic episode we join the club.

title: How to Drink a Tree's Blood
summary: Of course we're talking all about maple syrup today - the tapping, the processing, the eating.

title: Short Stuff: Wisdom Teeth
summary: By all rights there should be three sets of molars in your mouth. But it turns out that our skulls aren’t really set up to accommodate that many anymore. Exactly why depends on who you ask.

title: Save the Whales!
summary: In the 1970s, conservation groups around the world rose up to protect dwindling whale populations, some on the verge of extinction. They all worked under the same banner: Save the Whales! It turned out to be one of the most successful campaigns ever.

title: Selects: How Fever Dreams Work
summary: Fever dreams can be unsettling experiences. These ramped up nightmares are vivid, detailed and only happen when the human body experiences a fever. What is it about the combination of fevers and dreams that make these night terrors so hellish? Learn all that and more in this classic episode.

title: UNESCO World Heritage: Preserving the Best of Humanity
summary: Humanity’s created a lot of neat things over the eons and starting in the 1940s, the UN created an agency focused on preserving those things for the whole world and future people. But that mission is in danger of becoming only about branding and money.

title: Short Stuff: Brown-Headed Cowbird
summary: There’s a kind of bird that lots of people think is a real jerk. And it kind of is. But in the brown-headed cowbird’s defense, it’s just evolved that way. Find out why it has such a bad reputation among bird lovers in this Short Stuff.

title: Some Silly Inventions That Became Wildly Popular
summary: Once in a while someone comes up with a solution for a problem we didn’t know we had, and maybe even a problem that didn’t even exist. Even more rarely, the stars align just right so that some crackpot invention captures everyone’s imagination.

title: Selects: Sammy Davis Jr: National Treasure
summary: In this classic episode Josh and Chuck sit down and detail the complicated life of the late, great Sammy Davis Jr.

title: The Sewol Ferry Disaster
summary: In 2014 a ferry carrying hundreds of South Korean high school students on a field trip sunk, killing almost everyone on board. Hauntingly, their deaths were fully avoidable: everyone from the dock inspector to the Coast Guard to the president failed them.

title: Short Stuff: Cherry Blossoms
summary: The Japanese Cherry Blossom is a sight to behold. But how did they get to Washington D.C.?

title: Are Generations Even a Thing?
summary: We all love to tour our generation's superiority, but who decides where the split occurs and what to name it? And is this even a thing or just an arbitrary division?

title: Selects: What is a Numbers Station?
summary: If you think secretly coded messages sent via short wave radio is Cold War relic, think again. In this classic episode, Chuck and Josh are here to dispel that myth, along with many others relating to numbers stations, including why they might still be operational.

title: How Worker Co-ops Work
summary: The worker co-op has a rich tradition and can work a variety of ways. Join us as we dig into the nuts and bolts.

title: Short Stuff: History of Spring Break
summary: If you think Spring Break started with northern college kids heading to Florida to party, you'd be correct. But there's slightly more to it than that.

title: Roar: The Most Dangerous Movie Ever Made?
summary: Jump in today to hear all about the disaster that was the movie ROAR.

title: Selects: The Skinny on Lyme Disease
summary: If you live in the Northeastern U.S. then you may know someone who has had Lyme disease. But it's spreading all over the country and parts of the world. Learn all about this tick-borne disease in this classic episode.

title: The Colorado River Compact
summary: Deciding how to share water is pretty important stuff when there isn't much of it around. Today we dive into the Colorado River Compact.

title: Short Stuff: Simple Spelling Movement
summary: Pretty much everyone agrees that English is a chaotic language. There are nutso rules of grammar and spelling other languages don’t have. More than once, movements have emerged to simplify English and each time they were beaten back with a vengeance.

title: The Middle Class: Canary in the Gold Mine
summary: Lots of nations gauge the health of their country by how the middle class is doing. There’s just one issue with that – no one can say exactly what defines the middle class. But even when you take a guess, it seems like the health isn’t so good these days.

title: Selects: The Disappearance of Lars Mittank
summary: In 2014, a young German man walked into an airport in Bulgaria with a flight booked, then suddenly ran out leaving all his posessions behind, never to be heard from again. This classic episode tells the story of Lars Mittank.

title: Malcom X
summary: Malcolm X was one of the most revered, feared leaders of the civil rights movement. In contrast to Martin Luther King, Jr., X advocated black self-reliance and separateness in American society and that equal rights should obtained by any means necessary.

title: Short Stuff: Kentucky Meat Shower
summary: In 1876 it rained meat out of the clear blue sky on a homestead in Bath County, Kentucky. While the mystery of what happened will never be solved, the best explanation makes the story even weirder than it seems.

title: The History of Fire
summary: The first fires came from lightning strikes. After that, no one is super sure when we started controlling it and then later, starting our own. But it's sure fun to speculate!

title: Selects: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About Gin
summary: If there's one thing we've learned about Chuck over the years it's that he loves his gin. And he loves it even more now that understands it. Pour yourself a martini and cozy up to the classic gin-cast.

title: Caterpillars: Nature's Magicians
summary: Caterpillars are simply the best. Don't think so? Well listen in and you'll soon agree.

title: Butterflies: Caterpillars with Wings!
summary: If you thought caterpillars were awesome, just wait until you see them with colorful, iridescent wings!

title: How Snails Work
summary: They seem gross and bothersome at first, but once you get down to ground level and get to know snails, we’ll bet you’ll grow quite fond of them. They are living in a whole world we’re largely unaware of.

title: The Fascinating History of Dandelions
summary: Dandelions are way more interesting than you think. Trust us and click play.

title: What's Permaculture All About?
summary: Permaculture is a growing trend in the world of farming and home landscaping. It's basically a design principle that emphasizes sustainability and the would-be, natural ecosystem of an area. Simple concepts like planting downhill from a pond and using gravity to feed plants to planting native plants and vegetation that work well together are hallmarks of permaculture. Learn all about this eco-friendly trend today.

title: How Sneezing Works
summary: Unless you have an arcane disorder from a lesion on a very specific spot on our medulla, the chances are you sneeze. Turns out most animals do it, even lizards! Learn the whys and hows of this most interesting involuntary reflex.

title: Wetlands! Wetlands! Wetlands!
summary: It’s time to get jazzed up for some Earth science of the waterlogged variety. Join Chuck and Josh as they tour some of the most interesting ecosystems on the planet and learn why we need to stop destroying them post haste.

title: Composting: Nature's Most Interesting Process
summary: You may think composting is just a bunch of old banana peels rotting away into dirt but, friend, you're not looking closely enough. Inside that compost pile is a microcosmic universe doing some magical stuff.

title: Squirrels, Ahoy!
summary: Squirrels are rodents, sure, but they’re rodents with personalities the size of Las Vegas and Detroit put together. Get to know your bushy-tailed (and sometimes not so bushy) neighbors who live interesting hidden lives right out in the open.

title: Honey: Nature's Wonder Sugar
summary: Honey is an amazing thing. Just ask any bee. They make a ton of it. So much that humans get what bees can't use and that's a lot of honey.

title: Contortionism: Bend It Like Gumby
summary: If you could put your leg behind your head, would you? Of course you would! You might even make a career out of it, amazing people around the world with your flexibility. That’d make you a contortionist! But first you’d better get started with stretching.

title: Short Stuff: Jeddah Tower
summary: The Jeddah Tower is set to be the tallest building in the world. If it ever gets finished.

title: Ruth Lyons: TV Pioneer
summary: Ruth Lyons basically invented the daytime talk show, yet she doesn't get the credit. Why is that? Probably because she was a woman in a man's industry. Today we tell her story.

title: Selects: Mangroves: Nature's Best Tree?
summary: Mangroves are incredible survivors and adapters. They're also amazing at lessening the impact of tropical storms and climate change. And heck, they're cool looking. So jump into the brackish waters and have a listen to this classic episode all about these beauts.

title: How the Kowloon Walled City Worked
summary: From the 1970s to the early 1990s a patch of land in Hong Kong the size of just a few football fields was the most densely-populated area in the world – and by a longshot. Even more remarkable, it was an outlaw land that somehow formed a tight community.

title: Short Stuff: In-Flight Entertainment
summary: Movies on planes have changed a lot in the last couple of decades. Today, we'll go over how this stuff works.

title: The Fyre Festival Fiasco
summary: What happens when a career grifter tries to throw a "luxury" music festival in only six months? Not much it turns out.This was the Fyre Festival.

title: Selects: How Spiritualism Works
summary: Something spooky was born on the American frontier in the mid-19th century: the idea that people’s personalities survive death and that some gifted individuals can communicate with them. It developed into a religion that some still practice today.

title: Let's All Go to the World's Fair
summary: Before the internet could show you anything in the universe - including stuff it made up - people had few opportunities to have their minds blown. But every few years, somewhere in the world nations would gather and show off the cool stuff they invented.

title: Short Stuff: Johnny Ringo
summary: You might be familiar with the outlaw Johnny Ringo from the movie Tombstone. He was indeed a real-life black hat gunslinger, and a tragic figure at that.

title: The Gold Standard: When Money Meant Something
summary: There was a time less than 100 years ago when you could exchange your paper currency at the bank for actual gold. Gave folks a sense of stability, it did. Depending on your view, we either ruined or built our economies when money became just paper.

title: Selects: How Dopamine Works
summary: Dopamine is perhaps the most talked-about, most misunderstood biochemical in our bodies. It’s linked to not only addiction and depravity, but also focus, motivation, and living a productive life. How can one molecule be so many things to so many people? Find out all about it in this classic episode.

title: The Battle of the Sexes
summary: Back in 1973 a male chauvinist played tennis against champion Billie Jean King. This is that story.

title: Short Stuff: MacGuffins
summary: What’s a MacGuffin? We don’t know. No one knows. But it has to do with movies and that’s fun to talk about.

title: The Murder of Jane Stanford
summary: Stanford University was co-founded by Jane Stanford. Not long after she was murdered and it was covered up. We'll probably never know what really happened. Listen in today.

title: Selects: How Free Range Parenting Works
summary: Free range parenting is all about giving your child the freedom to play and explore life on their own. Are there benefits? Sure. Do some people hate the concept? Yes! Listen to this classic episode and learn right here.

title: How the Flexner Report Changed Medicine
summary: The Flexner Report shook up medicine in the United States when it was released in 1910 and it's never been the same since. For better or worse.

title: Short Stuff: Safety Coffins
summary: Back in the 1800s, people had an outsized fear of being buried alive. Enter... THE SAFETY COFFIN!

title: How Crowds Work
summary: If you’ve ever been out of your house you’ve probably been in a crowd before. They can be as mundane as an elevator full of people or as consequential as a mass of protesters. But did you know there’s psychology to crowds? And they follow fluid dynamics?

title: Selects: How Charles Darwin Worked
summary: Charles Darwin wasn't the first or only scientist to grasp the theory of evolution through natural selection, but he became its father and icon. In this classic episode, learn about the man who reluctantly but bravely became the source of the divide between religion and science.

title: How Lasers Work
summary: It turns out that lasers are even cooler than they look. And as far as acronyms go, they’re pretty solid in that respect too. There’s way too much cool stuff about lasers to tease here so listen to this old school SYSK episode and let lasers blow away.

title: Short Stuff: Aztec Death Whistle
summary: In the late 90s, a strange musical instrument was excavated under the streets of CDMX. Listen in to learn all about the Aztec Death Whistle.

title: How Cognitive Biases Work
summary: Humans have all sorts of weird quirks that cause us to do silly things and make bad decisions. It’s not our fault though. Our brains are wired that way. Learn about the psychology of cognitive biases in this episode.

title: Selects: Why Do Great Flood Myths Seem To Be Universal?
summary: If look into the mythology of just about any culture in the world, you will find a myth about a great flood that destroyed humanity and submerged the Earth in the distant past. Does this mean that a great flood actually happened? Listen to this classic episode to explore the possibilities with Josh and Chuck.

title: The Cajun Navy: Heroes or Liability?
summary: The Cajun Navy was formed after Hurricane Katrina and really got its legs after the Louisiana flood of 2016. They save a lot of lives, but some fear the pitfalls of "vigilante heroism." Learn all about this group of do-gooders today.

title: Short Stuff: Color Psychology
summary: Have you ever cried way longer than usual when you were in a yellow room? You’ve been smacked by color psychology my friend and it’s got your number.

title: Helen Keller and Anne Sullivan: Miracle is Right
summary: Helen Keller and Anne Sullivan were one of the most amazing non-magical duos in history. Imagine living trapped in your own mind – unable to see or hear – and then imagine learning to read, traveling the world, and becoming an ambassador of peace.

title: Selects: Operation Mincemeat: How A Corpse Fooled the Nazis
summary: In World War II, a secret department of British 'corkscrew thinkers' hatched a plan to use the cadaver of an unclaimed homeless man to turn the tide of the war in the Allies' favor. It worked. Listen to this classic episode as Josh and Chuck take you through the real life tale.

title: The Magnificent Golden Gate Bridge
summary: If you think the Golden Gate Bridge is named because of its color then you are wrong. That name proceeds the bridge by a long time. But that’s just one interesting fact about this amazing structure. Tune in today.

title: Short Stuff: Magic 8 Ball
summary: The Magic 8 Ball, the mystical fortune telling pool ball started out as a piece of customer swag for the Brunswick Billiard Company. Since then, it has changed the course of history and shaped nations.

title: The Charge of the Light Brigade
summary: The Charge of the Light Brigade is a famous poem about a lesser famous military action during the Crimean War. Tune in today for a rare SYSK walk through wartime history.

title: Selects: The Truth Behind Cage-Free and Free-Range
summary: You’d think terms like cage-free and free-range means the chickens we eat are frolicking happily in the fresh air under the shining sun, but you’d be so, so wrong. Cage-free is a huge improvement but free-range is lacking and both have a long way to go. Find out all about both in this classic episode.

title: The Ballad of Biggie and Tupac
summary: Biggie Smalls and Tupac Shakur had a famous beef with one another in the mid-90s. It was so intense, it sparked an even wider rivalry between the East and West Coasts. In just a few years, both men had been murdered and the music world was changed forever.

title: Short Stuff: The S7VEN Deadly Sins
summary: The Seven Deadly Sins are tied to religion, but not really in the Bible. So where did this naughty list come from?

title: Keeping Time
summary: Today, Chuck and Josh walk you through the history of keeping time, from sticks in the sun to atomic clocks.

title: Selects: BPD: The Worst Disorder or Not a Disorder at All?
summary: Borderline Personality Disorder has been described as emotional “third degree burns over ninety percent of your body.” It’s as close to a curse as a personality disorder can be: deep fear of being abandoned creates behaviors that end up driving people off. Learn all about it in this classic episode.

title: Data Centers: Can't Live With Em, Can't Live Without Em
summary: Data centers are the backbone of our digital world. All the sites you visit and social media you post happen there. A boom in huge data centers to support AI is underway, and they’re taking a big toll on the environment and life for the people around them.

title: Short Stuff: Did a vampire legend help win the Cold War?
summary: During the Cold War, the CIA used the legend of a vampire named Aswang to scare locals into not helping the communists.

title: Doin’ Science in the National Radio Quiet Zone
summary: West Virginia is home to sensitive radio telescopes that could easily pick up your cell phone’s signal on Mars. And the cell reception on Mars is about as good as it is in the NRQZ, since cell towers are banned in the interest of furthering astronomy.

title: Selects: How Forgiveness Works
summary: For most of history, forgiveness fell under the domain of religion. But in the 1980s science started investigating it and found that forgiving someone is really, really good for you. Learn how anybody can be the better person in this classic, and really great, episode.

title: The SAD Episode
summary: Seasonal affective disorder, or SAD, is much more than the winter blues. It's a serious subset of depression. Learn all about it and what to do if you suffer from it today.

title: Short Stuff: Neighborhood Watch
summary: Since 1972 neighborhoods have been officially banding together to prevent crime together. Does it work? It seems to. Does it go too far? It often does, yes.

title: The Warrens: Paranormal Power Couple
summary: Today we dive into the interesting story of paranormal power couple the Warrens, inspiration behind The Conjuring movie franchise.

title: Selects: MC Escher and His Trippy Art
summary: We love us some MC Escher. Turns out his story is pretty fascinating too. Tune in to this classic episode and find out all about it with Josh and Chuck.

title: TV Moments That Changed The World
summary: Whatever you think of TV, you have to admit it has shaped the world (maybe more than the internet, according to Josh). There have been moments here or there in TV history where the world took a new course and we go over some of them in this episode.

title: Short Stuff: All About Porcelain
summary: What exactly is this durable ceramic anyway?

title: What We Lost When We Lost Home Ec
summary: Home economics seems antiquated – a class that teaches high school kids how to bake a cake and sew doesn’t sound super useful. But would you believe that everything from the obesity epidemic to student debt can be chalked up to home ec disappearing?

title: Selects: How Miniature Golf Works
summary: Playing miniature golf is a very fun thing to do and, you’re about to find, learning about its origin and history is very fun as well. Join Josh and Chuck in this classic episode as they tee off on the mini golf story!

title: Dolls and Dolls, Guys!
summary: In this special Christmas Day episode, we get cuddly with one of the all-time great holiday gifts, dolls! Where did they come from? Why are the so cute? Why are they sometimes creepy? Why do they tell us to do things we don’t want to with their minds?

title: Short Stuff: Why is holly a holiday thing?
summary: Holly is waxy and super sharp, not exactly the kind of thing you'd want all over your house. Yet it happens every holiday season. Today we dig in to discover why.

title: SYSK's 2025 Holiday Extravaganza Christmas Special
summary: Deck your tidings and get your halls nice and gladded because it’s time for maybe the best episode of the year, where SYSK loosens our ties, puts on our smoking jackets and Santa hats and create holiday nostalgia in real time. Happy holidays, everybody!

title: Selects: PT Barnum: More Complicated Than You've Heard
summary: When your life is as outsized as the World’s Greatest Showman PT Barnum it’s pretty easy to - you know - gloss over the grimmer aspects when you turn it into an uplifting musical movie. But the way to understand a person is to look at them, warts and all. Josh and Chuck take a full accounting in this classic episode.

title: Doggerland: Lost at Sea
summary: The story of Doggerland is pretty fascinating. The idea is that mainland Europe and the UK were connected not only by a land bridge, but a place where plants, animals and even humans, thrived.

title: Short Stuff: Battle of Itter Castle
summary: At the end of WWII in Europe, one of the strangest battles of the war took place between German troops fighting alongside Americans and French to beat back an assault by the Nazi SS.

title: Battle Royale: Optimists vs Pessimists
summary: Everybody’s always bagging on pessimists and telling everybody they should be more optimistic. Well, nuts to that! There are plenty of benefits from being a pessimist. Although being an optimist still wins in basically every category ☹

title: Selects: Star Wars Holiday Spectacular
summary: Long ago, in a galaxy not so far away, George Lucas allowed the Star Wars Holiday Special to be made. What happened on the night of November 17, 1978 can never be fully explained, but we make our best effort in our annual special edition of SYSK. May the force be with us all.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: What Makes a Must-Have Christmas Toy?
summary: Ever since Cabbage Patch Kids came along in 1983, there’s been an annual holiday frenzy around one particular toy – the must-have Christmas toy of the year. But what makes a toy a must-have toy? Josh and Chuck investigate (and kick off the holidays).

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: How Play-Doh Works
summary: Do you love Play-Doh? Chuck and Josh certainly love to talk about it, from its interesting history as a wall cleaner, to its more scientific chemical properties. It's everything you ever wanted to know about the pliable children's toy.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: How Yo-Yos Work
summary: You may have played with a yo-yo before -- perhaps you've even walked the dog -- but do you know about the physics behind what makes a yo-yo sleep and wake up? Learn all about inertia, angular momentum and the history of the yo-yo in this episode of SYSK.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: A Partial History of Action Figures
summary: Action figures have a long and glorious history. From GI Joes to Star Wars figures, these offshoots of dolls came along at just the right time to capture the hearts and minds of children everywhere. Learn all about the partial history of action figures right here.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: Cabbage Patch Kids: Must-Have Toy of the Century
summary: Surprisingly, Cabbage Patch Kids have turned up on SYSK almost as much as the Nazis or Seinfeld. It’s finally time to dive all the way into CPKs, from their controversial origins to the Christmas craze of ‘83 to their alter egos, Garbage Pail Kids.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: Hula-Hoops: The Toy That's A Shape
summary: We've covered our fair share of pop-culture icons and here is another - Hula-Hoops. They've been around since ancient time in some form or another, but made their name in during the Hoop Boom of the 1950s. Learn all about this popular fad and more.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: How Monopoly Works
summary: Since more than 1 billion people have played it, you're probably familiar with the board game Monopoly, but we bet you don't know its secret origins as a left-wing socialist teaching tool. Learn about the history, rules and cultural impact of Monopoly.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: Beanie Babies: Reigning Toy Craze Champion
summary: The world has seen a lot of weird investment bubbles in its time, but few of them rival the fever that gripped the world in the 90s after Beanie Babies took off. Let’s visit this strange chapter in toy history together.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: Etch A Sketch!
summary: The Etch A Sketch is yet another classic toy that Josh and Chuck love and respect. Learn all about this Hall of Fame entry today.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: How the Nintendo Entertainment System Changed Gaming Forever
summary: For the holidays in 1986 (and ’87) (and ’88) the most stupendous, most wanted, most amazing thing any kid could possibly get – outside of a pony, *maybe* – was the NES. That year, video games came back from the dead and changed forever.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: How Hot Wheels Work
summary: If you're an American who had a childhood, you probably have some nostalgia for Hot Wheels. Get your engines revved for this trip down memory lane as we discuss these fun and iconic toys.

title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: How Easy Bake Ovens Work
summary: Easy Bake Ovens are as iconic as a toy can get, as American as apple pie or baseball. Learn all about these light bulb cooking, working ovens that endanger children to this day, in this classic episode.

title: A Quick History of the BBC
summary: The BBC has been around as long as there has been radio. Today we salute the venerable institution that's as British as tea and crumpets.

title: Short Stuff: Atacama Skeleton
summary: In 2003, a tiny – really, really tiny – humanoid skeleton surfaced that had been taken from Chile. The only possible explanation is that it had to be an alien mummy. Right?

title: Operation Paul Bunyan
summary: If we told you that World War III was in danger of happening over the trimming of a tree would you believe us? This was Operation Paul Bunyan.

title: Selects: What Is A Mold-A-Rama?
summary: In the 1960s, a very cool machine debuted at the Seattle World's Fair - the Mold-A-Rama. It made real plastic toys on-demand from melted plastic pellets, to the delight of children and adults alike. They didn't last too long, but can still be found at various locations all over the United States and their retro-cool stylings are still a hit. Learn all about these cool machines in this classic episode.

title: What's the bar exam like anyway?
summary: You've always heard about "the bar" but what do you really know about it? Unless you've taken it, probably not much. Well join the club. Let's discuss.

title: Short Stuff: Camberley Kate
summary: Camberley Kate was the nickname for the first independent animal rescuer in England, rescuing hundreds of dogs and cats over her lifetime. Come get acquainted with a great lady!

title: The Brutal History of Prison Labor
summary: The idea of prison labor is relatively new in the annals of crime and punishment. And it's just as bad as you think.

title: Selects: How Black Friday Works
summary: On the day after Thanksgiving, Americans go kind of crazy for the deep discount sales that kick off the holiday shopping season in stores. So crazy, in fact, at least four people have lost their lives and as many as 63 others have been injured during Black Friday sales. But as profitable as Black Friday is, some retailers are thinking about discontinuing the tradition to find ways to make even more money. Learn all about this bizarre, uniquely American holiday custom in this classic episode.

title: Julia Child, la Grandes Gourmande
summary: Julia Child is one of the most recognizable names in the cooking world, but even still so many of her accomplishments aren’t widely known. And the impacts she had on American culture, whoa! Join Josh and Chuck as they savor the flavor of Julia Child!

title: Short Stuff: Pies
summary: We’ve done episodes on cake, cookies and, at long last, pie. Belly up to your pod player and prepare to crave some pie!

title: Rice is Nice
summary: Rice may be the most eaten food on the planet, accounting for 50% of the caloric intake of Asian countries and 25% worldwide. Learn all about this edible cereal crop today.

title: Selects: Rockettes: Still Kicking After All These Years
summary: Tune in to this classic episode to learn all about the legendary NYC Rockettes, who actually got their start in Missouri.

title: Graffiti: So Cool It’s A Pillar of Hip Hop
summary: Graffiti – the good kind, done with lots of style and skill – developed when some kids in NYC took up cans of spray paint and started to figure out how to outdo one another. They laid down styles that are so fine they’re still being used by artists today.

title: Short Stuff: Victorian Flower Language
summary: What do you do when you want to tell someone you’re smitten with them but you live in a society so repressive decorum prevents you from even speaking such things? Why, you can say it with flowers! And that’s just what people in the Victorian Era did.

title: AM Radio: Solid Gold
summary: The era of AM radio isn't over, but it's well past its heyday. Dive in today for a trip down memory lane.

title: Selects: How Personality Tests Work
summary: For millennia, we have tried to put human personalities into neat types, an effort psychology took up early in its history in an effort to legitimize itself. But is the idea of types – which all personality inventories are based on - flawed to begin with? Find out in this classic episode.

title: Pop Tarts: No Fruit Necessary
summary: Pop Tarts are a legendary breakfast treat in the United States. They're fruit-filled toaster pastries with very little fruit. But who cares right? It's all about that toasty goodness.

title: Short Stuff: Third Man Syndrome
summary: People who’ve found themselves in life-or-death situations with their endurance at its limit have reported sensing another presence with them, urging them to continue on and survive. No one knows what the heck is going on here but it sure is interesting.

title: Eco-Disasters 101: The Salton Sea
summary: In 1905, an engineering mistake created a brand new 400-square-mile sea (lake?) in the California desert. People made the most of it at first, but it didn’t take long to become a toxic brew that now threatens the health of anyone in breathing distance.

title: Selects: How Conversion Therapy Doesn't Work
summary: Conversion therapy is a misguided attempt by religious zealots to convert people from gay to straight. News flash - it doesn't work. Learn all about this abhorrent practice in this classic episode.

title: The Mystery of the Death Valley Germans
summary: In 1996, a small group of German tourists disappeared in Death Valley National Park without a trace. Fifteen years later, the tenacity of one man solved the case.

title: Short Stuff: "Peace" Pipes
summary: Did Native Americans really smoke peace pipes? Well yes and no. They smoked pipes for many reasons, sometimes to commemorate peace. But they never called them peace pipes.

title: What To Do With All This Nuclear Waste?
summary: You can make a case that it’s a little off-putting to learn the world doesn’t really have any idea what to do with the nuclear waste we’ve been generating for several decades. The best we’ve come up with so far is bury it real deep and forget about it.

title: Selects: How Extinction Works
summary: Scientists believe that 99% of the estimated 50 billion species that have ever lived on Earth have disappeared through extinction. This is a natural process typically, but it can also be cataclysmic and it's becoming clear we are amid a massive one. Find out more with Josh and Chuck in this classic episode.

title: SYSK's 2025 Shocktober Halloween Spooktacular
summary: Co-producer Ben knocked it out of the park again, taking the two classic horror stories we read for our annual Spooktacular - Caterpillars and The Deep Drowse – and creating a moody Halloween masterpiece for your spooky listening enjoyment. So enjoy it!

title: Short Stuff: The Bell Witch
summary: A legend in Tennessee tells of the real-life Bell family, who were haunted back in 1817 by a ghost witch - arguably the worst kind of either of those things.

title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre: Masterpiece
summary: There aren’t too many independent horror movies that make the British Film Institute’s 250 Best Films Ever Made list – AND – make an appearance in the teen comedy Summer School. That makes sense because there’s no other movie quite like The TCSM.

title: Selects: The Great Finger in the Wendy’s Chili Caper
summary: In 2005 a woman named Anna Alaya discovered a length of human finger – nail and all – in her Wendy’s chili. Her cries of disgust would set off a media firestorm, a criminal investigation and a prison sentence for her and her husband. Listen to Josh and Chuck go through the whole mess in this classic episode.

title: THE HUMAN SCREAM
summary: Have you ever thought much about screaming? Well we have, and today you'll learn everything we learned.

title: Short Stuff: Curse of Broken Mirrors
summary: It's seven years' bad luck for you if you break a mirror, buddy, sorry. But have you ever wondered why? People have come up with all sorts of great reasons since time immemorial.

title: [Insert Your Own Catchy Title About Younger Dryas Here]
summary: Quick, name your favorite geological mystery. You can’t do it! Well, don’t worry. In this episode we’re going to tell you all about what will surely be your favorite (albeit only) one when we get into one weird millennium that happened not that long ago.

title: Selects: How ESP Works (?)
summary: Even though almost half of Americans believe in it, ESP usually is treated as a load of bull by skeptics. But some respected researchers have dared to apply the scientific method to investigate ESP and a few have found some surprising results. Find out all about it with Josh and Chuck in this classic episode.

title: VH-1: MTV for Your Parents
summary: Today we complete our music video duology with a dive into the mellow pool of VH-1.

title: Short Stuff: China's Corpse Walkers
summary: If you died away from home but wanted to be buried there, don’t worry – Taoist priests had you covered. They’d just have your animated corpse walk itself back home.

title: We want our MTV!
summary: If you've ever wanted to hear a couple of Gen X'ers wax nostalgic about MTV, then you're in luck.

title: Selects: How Schoolhouse Rock Rocked: Featuring Bob Nastanovich of Pavement
summary: Schoolhouse Rock is possibly the best children's program of all time. Join Josh and Chuck in this classic episode as they tell the story of SR, featuring an interview with Pavement's Bob Nastanovich, contributor to the '90s Schoolhouse Rock tribute record.

title: Everyone Deserves A Good Death
summary: The concept of hospice was created as a way to help people with only a few weeks to live spend their last days comfortable an surrounded by friends and family in the hope they can pass away peacefully. It’s kind of crazy hospice was ever a radical idea.

title: Short Stuff: The Call is Coming... FROM INSIDE THE HOUSE
summary: Did you know that the "the call is coming from inside the house" urban legend may be based on a very grisly murder case from the 1950s?

title: The Happy Place of Saturday Morning Cartoons
summary: The greatest period in the history of humankind took place in the short era between 1970 and 1995. During that time kids could tune in every Saturday morning between 8 and noon and find the most amazing cartoons ever created, plus tons and tons of ads.

title: Selects: How Mail Order Marriages Work
summary: Everybody knows mail order marriages are at best a last resort for jerks looking to boss a foreign spouse around or, at worst, a front for human trafficking. Or are they? Yes and no. Mail order marriage comes with nuance and a surprisingly long history. Learn all about it in this classic episode.

title: The Mystery of the Sleepy Sickness
summary: Back in the early 1900s, a new pandemic happened out of nowhere with odd symptoms, that was never solved or cured. It just went away. Which means it's right up our alley.

title: Short Stuff: La Lechuza - The Witch Owl
summary: Today we kick off the scariest month with the legend of La Lechuza - The Witch Owl.

title: Why Would Anyone Want to Appease Hitler?
summary: It seems ridiculously irresponsible with the benefit of hindsight, but the concept of giving Hitler everything he wanted was the policy among the UK and France as a way to keep the world from sliding into a second world war. Turns out it didn’t work.

title: Selects: How Area 51 Works
summary: The secret military base Area 51 is inextricably linked to every secret, shady project the US government is rumored to be involved in – from reverse-engineering alien technology to coordinating a one-world government. The truth is much more mundane. Listen to this classic episode as Josh and Chuck break it down.

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Hinterkaifeck Axe Murders
summary: In 1922, a little farm in the woods of Bavaria became the site of what would become Germany’s most famous unsolved murder, when six people were brutally killed with a pick axe. What led up to it and followed is nothing short of bizarre.

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: SYSK Live: The DB Cooper Heist
summary: Join Josh and Chuck live from Seattle as they (sky)dive into one of the most brazen robberies in the annals of crime and the only unsolved airline hijacking in American history.

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: Who Committed the 1912 Villisca Ax Murders?
summary: In a small town in Iowa in 1912 eight people were murdered in the grisliest of ways while they slept. Local reputations were ruined when accusations flew, but could a drifting serial killer working across the Midwest have been behind it?

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Tylenol Murders, Part I
summary: On one terrible day in Chicago in 1982, seven people died suddenly and mysteriously. In just a matter of hours, it becomes clear, someone has poisoned bottles of Extra-Strength Tylenol, one of the most trusted and widely-used products in America.

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Chowchilla Bus Kidnapping
summary: The largest ever kidnapping case in the United States went down in the small town of Chowchilla, CA. Learn all about it today.

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Tylenol Murders, Part II
summary: The panic that began in Chicago spreads and begins to change the world. The investigation into the murders turns up leads and suspects, but still no one has ever been charged with the murders. It remains unsolved to this day. Find out the extent of what we know in this classic episode.

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Tale of the Bloody Benders
summary: Long before we knew what serial killers were, a family in remote Kansas was disposing of victims at their family farm. Listen in to the Tale of the Bloody Benders if you dare!

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Harvey’s Casino Bombing of 1980
summary: In August of 1980 a bomb containing 1,000 pounds of dynamite was quietly delivered to Harvey’s, a casino and resort at Lake Tahoe. This kicked off a whirlwind caper that lasted 30 hours and ended up nearly demolishing the 11-story resort.

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Strange Unsolved Murder of Ken McElroy
summary: The murder of Ken McElroy comes off like a story from a cheap paperback book you’d get to read on a plane. But this is a true crime story, set in Missouri in the early 80s. And boy does it pack a punch.

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Harrowing Story of the North Hollywood Shootout
summary: Tune in today to listen to the story of when North Hollywood became a war zone after a brazen bank robbery.

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Unsolved Indiana Dunes Disappearances
summary: In July 1966, three women out for a day at the beach waded into the water of Lake Michigan, got onto a boat and were never heard from again. To this day, not a trace of them has ever turned up and theories of what became of them abound.

title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: How The Great Train Robbery Worked
summary: In 1963, 15 men got together in England to pull off one of the most daring heists in history. The Great Train Robbery was the crime of the century, capturing the public's attention and leaving them torn on who to root for - the cops or the robbers. Learn all about England's greatest heist in today's episode.

title: A Tribute To The Far Side
summary: The Far Side is one of the greatest cartoons in history. Today we go to great lengths to convince you of that.

title: Short Stuff: Death Cap Mushroom
summary: The death cap mushroom lives up to its name. It’s a mushroom cap that causes death. Find out why.

title: Tdhtdhtdhtdhtdh: Sound Effects!
summary: Sound effects are one of the unsung parts of any movie or TV show – they’re best when you don’t even notice them making what you see on screen even more real, and when they’re off you notice immediately. Learn how hard this amazing craft is in this episode.

title: Selects: Slime Mold: 0% Mold, 100% Amazing
summary: If you’ve ever wandered past what looked like a pile of dog barf on a log during a hike in the woods, you’d just seen slime mold - one of the most perplexing organisms on Earth. Listen to this classic episode and get as amazed as Josh and Chuck were when they recorded it.

title: The Tuskegee Syphilis Experiment
summary: As part of our shameful history series, today we dive into the Tuskegee Syphilis Experiments of the 1930s, 40s, 50s, 60s and into the 70s.

title: Short Stuff: Killing a Dead Body
summary: If you try to kill someone who was already dead is that a bad thing? Yeah? How bad?

title: What was the Four Pests Campaign?
summary: Say one thing about Mao's communist China, they could kill some sparrows. Learn why and how in today's episode.

title: Selects: What's the deal with subpoenas?
summary: Subpoenas are all the rage. But what do they even mean if someone can just ignore it? Learn this and a lot more in this classic episode.

title: You’re So Good At Conversation!
summary: It’s an understated miracle that humans can get across ideas to one another by saying things out loud. We’re strangely good at not constantly talking over each other, interrupting one another, and correcting misunderstandings. All just by conversing!

title: Short Stuff: North Sentinel Island
summary: One of the last uncontacted people in the world live in the Bay of Bengal and they have made it clear they don’t want you to visit.

title: The Man with the Golden Arm
summary: Aussie James Harrison gave blood close to 1,200 times over a 60 year period and saved 2.5 million babies in the process. That makes him a hero.

title: Selects: Noise Pollution: Arrrgh!
summary: If you’ve ever found your blood pressure rising because some guy down the street doesn’t know how to keep the trigger on a leaf blower pulled all the way, then you’ve experienced noise pollution. Not only is it annoying, it turns out it’s deadly too! Learn all about it in this classic episode.

title: America’s Militarized Police
summary: In the 1960s, America took stock of itself when scores of low-income cities broke out in riots. It found that racism was at the root of many social problems. Instead of addressing the underlying issues, the country decided instead to militarize the police.

title: Short Stuff: The Mpemba Effect
summary: Why does water seem to freeze faster when it starts out warmer?

title: How Dolphins Work!
summary: E-e-e-eek! E-e-e-eek, we say! Adding to the tradition of our wonderful animal episodes we contribute this amazing installment on one of the all-time great sea creatures, the dolphin! Attach a sponge to your rostrum and dive in with Josh and Chuck!

title: Selects: What Were the BONE WARS?
summary: A pair of old timey fossil hunters had a rootin’ tootin’ rivalry that spilled from academic journals into the American Wild West - where fossils were dynamited and employees turned double agent. Learn about the two-fisted origins of American paleontology in this classic episode.

title: What are Blue Zones?
summary: Blue zones are areas where people supposedly have more 100+ year-olds than average. But is it all based on faulty records?

title: Short Stuff: 1561 Celestial Event
summary: An amazing case of an early modern mass sighting of UFOs came in Nuremberg, Germany in 1561. Except it wasn’t that at all.

title: The History of Orthodontics
summary: Crooked teeth have always been a thing, but it took us a long time to do something about it. Learn about the twisted history of orthodontics today!

title: Selects: The Flannen Isles Mystery
summary: In December 1900 three lighthouse keepers vanished without a trace from a deserted island in Scotland. To this day no one knows exactly what happened to them. Find out all about this strange situation in this classic episode.

title: Private Equity: Your Ears Will Bleed
summary: Private equity is a business operation where companies are bought and run at their leanest to maximize returns for a handful of investors. It can be a lifeline for a flailing company or run it into the ground. Either way, PE firms make out like bandits.

title: Short Stuff: The Lost (?) Continent of Lemuria
summary: Why aren't there lemurs in Africa? That question created a whole theory about a lost continent. Turns out it's not true.

title: The Unsolved Murder of Hall and Mills
summary: In 1922, a pastor and his mistress were murdered in New Jersey. Nobody was ever convicted of the crime even though it seems clear who did it.

title: Selects: How Rape Kits Work
summary: Rape kits are simple forensic evidence collection kits used when someone is sexually assaulted. But the story is deeper than this. Learn all about rape kits, the sad backlog problem, and what you can do to help, in this classic episode.

title: Heavy Metal Pt II
summary: In part two of Heavy Metal Week Josh and Chuck break down how specialized heavy metal music has become, talk about some of the great album covers, look at how metal hits the brain, and explain the sad death of guitar great Randy Rhoads.

title: Short Stuff: Devil Horns
summary: Metal fans have many ways to express themselves, but none are as metal as throwing the devil horns. But who did it first?

title: Heavy Metal Pt I
summary: Some of the most talented musicians in the world play heavy metal, some of the hardest-hitting music ever made. In this episode Chuck and Josh wade into the history of the genre, and try to get to the bottom of where the name came from.

title: Selects: The Disappearance of Flight MH370, Part II
summary: In the absence of an official explanation of why flight MH 370 disappeared in 2014, conjecture and conspiracy theories have filled the vacuum. Find out the current state of things in this classic episode.
