summary: You know all of those cords and cables and wires that we use to connect our stuff to the electrical grid so they’ll, you know, work? Imagine a day when energy flies through the air like wifi, utterly cord-free. Well, imagine no more! That day is coming!

title: Short Stuff: Smudging: Not just for hippies
summary: Smudging is the process of wafting around the smoke of burning white sage. What is it good for? Listen in and find out.

title: Haile Selassie: Statesman, Colonizer, God?
summary: If you grew up outside of Africa, you might know Haile Selassie’s name from reggae music - the man who ruled Ethiopia is considered a god in Jamaica. In Ethiopia opinions are more varied.

title: Selects: How Zero Population Growth Works
summary: In 1968, Paul Erlich published The Population Bomb, predicting coming famine and mass death. Erlich's predictions didn't pan out but his ideas launched a debate still raging today. Learn all about it in this classic episode.

title: The Story of the Nuclear Boy Scout
summary: David Hahn was a kid who was really into science. So much that he built a nuclear reactor in his mother's potting shed. And it worked.

title: Short Stuff: Benin Bronzes
summary: One of the world’s cultural treasure troves were created in West Africa. But for over a century they’ve been held in museums outside of Africa. In fact, an estimated 95 percent of Africa’s cultural heritage is kept in museums overseas.

title: Ray and Charles Eames: More than Chairs
summary: Charles and Ray Eames were superstar designers who dreamed up some of the most iconic pieces of furniture ever made. And they did much more than that.

title: Selects: Geodesic Domes: The Wave of the Future That Wasn't
summary: Sometimes a good idea doesn’t pan out in real life. Take Buckminster Fuller’s geodesic dome: It requires less energy to heat and cool, it’s cheap, and it’s durable enough to withstand a hurricane – but it’s also godawful ugly and that was its undoing. Learn more with Josh and Chuck in this classic episode.

title: Like, here's the episode on "like"
summary: Like is a very divisive word. Purists think it's like, a filler word born in the 80s that's like, destroying the English language. Turns out none of these are like, true.

title: Short Stuff: The Original Snake Oil Salesman
summary: There’s a great origin story behind snake oil salesmen, and it has to do with just one guy who singlehandedly gave it a bad name.

title: What Americans Ate When There Were No Food Laws
summary: There was a brief period in America’s history – after people left the farm to work in the city and before the government started regulating it – when there was a total, lawless free-for-all in the food industry. Things were bad. Really, really bad.

title: Selects: The Unabomber: Misguided to say the least
summary: The Unabomber was one of the most notorious and longest lasting cases in the history of the FBI. Just because the manifesto reads like he was a fortune teller doesn't make his actions any less deplorable. Learn all about this fascinating case in this classic episode.

title: What's the Pygmalion Effect?
summary: Do teachers and managers give special treatment to those who they're told have great academic or professional promise? Does this create a self-fulfilling prophecy, regardless of the truth? That's just part of the fascinating Pygmalion Effect.

title: Short Stuff: School Bus Yellow
summary: Why are all school buses the same color? Because one man made it so. This is that story.

title: Clue(do): Third Best Board Game Ever
summary: Whether you know it as Clue or Cluedo, the whodunnit mystery board game is one of the best of all time. Learn all about the history behind the game’s development, and strategies on how to crush your fellow players as soundly as Chuck’s wife crushes him.

title: Selects: How Disgust Works
summary: Disgust is an odd thing. It makes sense that we would feel a sense of revulsion at the thought of putting rotten meat in our mouths – that’s pure evolution. But why would we feel the same emotion at the thought of weird sex or from hearing a racist rant? Find out more in this classic episode.

title: The History of Las Vegas
summary: How did the sleepy Nevada town of Las Vegas become LAS VEGAS? Well, we'll let you know over the course of about 45 minutes.

title: Short Stuff: Wainscoting: When Half a Wall is Enough
summary: Wainscoting is a beloved and time-tested decorative way to spruce up your walls. But what is it anyway? Listen in to find out.

title: The Harrowing Story of the North Hollywood Shootout
summary: Tune in today to listen to the story of when North Hollywood became a war zone after a brazen bank robbery.

title: Selects: A List Of Games You Would Surely Lose to a Computer
summary: We live in a time where computers can beat the best humans in the world at chess, checkers, poker and video games. But these games are really just demonstrations of how intelligent our machines are growing. They’re growing more intelligent by the hour. This classic episode features a special guest, Tech Stuff's Jonathan Strickland.

title: Esperanto: Tre Mojosa
summary: One thing you could do is create your own language. Some people do and for lots of different reasons. LL Zamenhof created Esperanto to try to bring about world peace. It worked, but on a less-than-global scale.

title: Short Stuff: Hot Cold Plunge
summary: Jumping into a cold pool after a long sauna or hot tub can be pretty great. Saunas have proven health benefits like lowering blood pressure; cold plunges are shown to reduce inflammation. Why not combine them? A bunch of safety reasons, bucko, that’s why.

title: The Strange Unsolved Murder of Ken McElroy
summary: The murder of Ken McElroy comes off like a story from a cheap paperback book you’d get to read on a plane. But this is a true crime story, set in Missouri in the early 80s. And boy does it pack a punch.

title: Selects: Is yogurt a miracle food?
summary: Yogurt has been touted as a health food, but is it? Maybe. If you eat it every day. We get into the rich and creamy history of this supposed miracle food in today's episode. Get an earful of the stuff in this classic episode.

title: Jonestown
summary: We all know what happened at Jonestown, but who was Jim Jones before the tragedy at the People's Temple?

title: Short Stuff: Frozen Dead Guy
summary: Back in 1994, Nederland, Colorado found out it had a resident it hadn’t accounted for.

title: Dry Cleaning: Not Really Dry(!)
summary: Dry cleaning is one of those things that we’re all familiar with but don’t actually know much about. That will hold true no more! Learn about all the ins and outs of the dry cleaning biz, some of its toxic secrets, and some spot removal tips too!

title: Selects: History's Greatest Traitors
summary: The annals of history hold a special place for people who have carried out treachery and betrayed their own. Thousands of years later, their names are still synonymous with being a scoundrel around the world. From Marcus Brutus to Vidkun Quisling and more, in this classic episode Josh and Chuck examine some of the bigger turncoats to live -- and exonerate others.

title: How Cranes Work
summary: You’ve probably seen cranes moving elegantly in the sky, but did you know what an important role they play in their surroundings? Learn all about cranes in this episode on cranes.

title: Short Stuff: NYT Bestseller List
summary: What kind of black magic goes into deciding who makes the NYT Bestseller List? Well you probably don't know the whole story unless you work there.

title: Kenton Grua: Grand Canyon Legend
summary: Tune in today to listen to the amazing story of Colorado River guide Kenton Grua's wild 277 mile record-breaking speed run down the center of the Grand Canyon.

title: Selects: Dr. Seuss: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
summary: The Seuss is loose in this episode about legendary children's book author Ted Geisel. The funny thing is, he didn't ever want children of his own, and his past work was a bit problematic. Explore his entire legacy in this classic episode.

title: The 2000 Presidential Election: A Real Cluster
summary: When George W Bush and Al Gore ran against one another, most pundits predicted a tight race. Absolutely zero of them predicted the election would come down to a few hundred votes. Today, we still don’t know who won.

title: Short Stuff: Blueprints
summary: The story of why blueprints were blue is more involved than you think. It involves a chemical process and the Prussian Army. Yeah you heard me right.

title: SYSK Live in Nashville: The Biosphere II Experiment
summary: Hello, friends! Join us today for our annual live show release, recorded in beautiful Nashville. On the docket? The Biosphere II Experiment!

title: Selects: Nuclear Semiotics: How to Talk to Future Humans
summary: The nuclear waste we produce will be dangerous for a very long time. We’ve figured out how to safely store it in the earth until it’s no longer a biohazard. Now we just have to figure out how to warn humans 10,000 years in the future to stay away from it. Find out about our best ideas in this classic episode.

title: How Primitive Will Our Descendants Find Us?
summary: It’s all fun and games to think about how backwards and misguided some things people did in the past were until you realize we’ll be “the past” one day. What do we do now that will seem primitive then and how will they be better in the future?

title: Short Stuff: Scheele's Green
summary: Can you imagine a color so alluring that even though you know it’s toxic you’d still use it to your heart’s content? The Victorians certainly could.

title: How Snails Work
summary: They seem gross and bothersome at first, but once you get down to ground level and get to know snails, we’ll bet you’ll grow quite fond of them. They are living in a whole world we’re largely unaware of.

title: Selects: How Fireplaces Work
summary: They are dirty, harmful to your health, bad for the environment and utterly charming. Wood-burning fireplaces have been with us for centuries and, despite their many drawbacks, are sticking around. Learn more than you thought possible about the fireplace, in this classic episode.

title: The 2023 SYSK Ho-Ho-Holiday Spectacular!
summary: Happy Holidays, friends! Tune in today to listen to our annual ad-free holiday extravaganza. There will be talk of merriment and joy!

title: Short Stuff: Christmas Lights
summary: Just three years after the lightbulb was invented a compadre of Thomas Edison thought to use them to decorate his Christmas tree. It set off a sensation that’s gotten more popular each year since.

title: Beanie Babies: Reigning Toy Craze Champion
summary: The world has seen a lot of weird investment bubbles in its time, but few of them rival the fever that gripped the world in the 90s after Beanie Babies took off. Let’s visit this strange chapter in toy history together.

title: Selects: Star Wars Holiday Spectacular
summary: Long ago, in a galaxy not so far away, George Lucas allowed the Star Wars Holiday Special to be made. What happened on the night of November 17, 1978 can never be fully explained, but we make our best effort in our annual special edition of SYSK. May the force be with us all.

title: Selects: How Dictators Work
summary: There are many types of dictators, from so called "benevolent" ones to the kind who rule with an iron fist. There are also many ways they can come into power, and they don't all include violence. Learn all about dictators past and present in this classic episode.

title: What was the Skeleton Army?
summary: The Skeleton Army was a rowdy group of folks in England who battled, sometimes violently, with the Salvation Army - largely against their efforts to keep people from drinking and having a rowdy good time. Listen in today!

title: Short Stuff: Pickles
summary: Josh loves pickles but hates cucumbers. Chuck loves cucumbers but hates pickles. WHO WILL WIN?

title: The Matewan Massacre
summary: The Matewan Massacre was a pivotal moment for the US mining industry and the labor movement as a whole. Learn about what happened in this sleepy West Virginia town today.

title: Selects: What were the Freedom Schools?
summary: Freedom Schools were set up in Mississippi in the heart of the Civil Rights Movement, with the aim of giving young black school children agency and a future. They remain one of the more inspiring and progressive programs in American History, yet so few know about them. We're hoping to change that. Learn all about them in this classic episode.

title: The Murder of John Lennon
summary: On December 8th, 1980, John Lennon was shot and killed outside his apartment building in New York City, by Mark David Chapman. Music history was altered forever. Listen in to this tragic story.

title: Short Stuff: Boba Tea
summary: Boba tea is bubble tea. But what are the bubbles? Tapioca pearls! Listen in today to learn about the disputed history of this trendy beverage.

title: The Life and Works of J.D. Salinger
summary: J.D. Salinger was a complicated and problematic human who stopped publishing soon after creating one of the great works of literature. Listen in today to learn the good, bad and ugly sides of the man who got famous, then dropped out.

title: Selects: Beavers: Tail Slapping Fun
summary: Beavers are in fact, very busy. They're builders and solid family members, husbands and wives. Learn all about N America's largest rodent in this classic episode.

title: You Down With OED?
summary: The story of the Oxford English Dictionary is really something. From its origin to its crowd-sourced literary quotations. Dive in today to learn all about the best dictionary.

title: Short Stuff: The Zipper Merge
summary: When you switch lanes on the highway after noticing that the lane you’re in is ending up ahead, you are literally ruining the world.

title: Plate Tectonics Are What Makes Earth Inhabitable
summary: It’s time to get jazzed about Earth science again. It’s only been 60 or so years since we’ve known the continents move around and we’re still figuring out exactly how they do. But one thing is for sure, that super-slow movement is super important.

title: Selects: NYC Water: An Engineering Marvel
summary: Getting the rain and melted snow from upstate NY into the taps of every NYC resident and business is one of the great feats of engineering. Does it taste great and make perfect bagels and pizza crust? Sources say yes! Learn all about it in this classic episode.

title: The Wreck of the Costa Concordia
summary: It’s astounding that with the exceptional navigational equipment aboard a cruise ship can run aground in the 21st century, and 32 passengers and crew can lose their lives within a thousand feet of land. Such is the power of incompetence and cowardice.

title: Short Stuff: Magnetic Pole Switcheroo
summary: Everyone once in a while, say a few hundred thousand years or so, the north and south poles of Earth’s magnetic field switch places. The result: Dogs and cats living together.

title: Legs! Legs! Legs! (The Periodic Table)
summary: If you’ve ever wanted to listen to two totally untrained, non-chemists who are fully unqualified to explain how the periodic table works nervously explain how the periodic table works, then this episode is for you. Chemistry majors, be warned.

title: Selects: E.T.: Is It Really the Worst Video Game of All Time?
summary: If you play video games you probably have an easy answer to worst game of all time: ET. But it turns out there are no easy answers, especially when you’re talking about a game so terrible it’s blamed for bringing the entire video game industry with it. Find out more in this classic episode.

title: Diners: The Most American Establishment?
summary: Diners may just be the most American establishment there is. They were born in the USA, thanks to European immigrants, and they only exist in the USA, unless it's a kitschy homage. So break open that 12-page menu and order up.

title: Short Stuff: Liberty Bell
summary: The story of the Liberty Bell is far more confusing than we imagined.

title: The Tragic Death of Natalie Wood
summary: Natalie Wood was Hollywood royalty who tragically drowned after a long night of partying with her husband, Robert Wagner, and actor Christopher Walken. Over the last 40 plus years, stories have changed and the investigation has moved from closed to open. Listen in to learn this tragic story.

title: Selects: Who were the Buffalo Soldiers?
summary: Josh and Chuck dive into history in this classic episode to tell the story of the Buffalo Soldiers.

title: How Scuba Works
summary: It’s a good, old fashioned how it works episode where we break down all of the nuts and bolts and threats to safety that make scuba diving such a unique and thrilling hobby. Dive in feet first with Josh and Chuck on the undersea adventure of a lifetime!

title: Short Stuff: Petrified Wood
summary: Petrified wood isn't just hard wood. Listen in today to learn all about this unique process.

title: Things We Believed Before the Scientific Method
summary: It’s easy to think of people in the distant past as kinda dumb for believing things like that mice could spontaneously generate from old grain. But if you look a little deeper, you’ll find there was a sensibility to the odd beliefs that came before science.

title: Selects: Are Election Laws Designed to Suppress Voting?
summary: Are laws that are meant to protect the sanctity of the polling place in reality designed to make it harder for groups that traditionally vote Democrat to cast their ballots? Find out in this classic episode.

title: The Harlem Globetrotters: American Treasures
summary: The Harlem Globetrotters are an American entertainment institution. Their story may not be quite what you think either. Hint, they didn't originate in Harlem. Tune in now to learn their fun, fascinating story.

title: Short Stuff: White Dog Poop
summary: If you grew up from the 70s to the 90s you know white dog poop. It’s the old, crusty – yes, white – phase that dog poop goes through as it ages on a lawn. Or it used to. Where has all the white poop gone?

title: The 14th Annual Halloween Spooktacular!
summary: As per tradition, today Josh and Chuck perform a spooky Halloween story reading to delight, amuse and FRIGHTEN YOU TO YOUR CORE. Will Meagle show up? Tune in to find out! Thanks to guest producer Ben Hackett for all the great sound effects.

title: Selects: How Mummies Work
summary: A mummy is a human being whose soft tissue has been preserved after death, and there are mummies around the world -- including natural mummies, as well as corpses that have been intentionally embalmed. Listen to this classic episode with Chuck and Josh to learn more.

title: Naked Mole Rats: A Face Only a Mother Could Love
summary: Naked mole rats are funny looking to be sure, but neither moles nor rats. So what are they? You'll have to tune in to find out.

title: Short Stuff: Bed Sheet Ghosts
summary: The simple bed sheet has provided countless kids and adults with an easy go-to Halloween costume. But why do we associate white sheets with ghosts anyway?

title: The Compton Cafeteria Riot
summary: Three years before the riots at Stonewall, the LGBTQ community of San Francisco's Tenderloin rose up. And the story was almost lost to time. Learn how and why today.

title: Selects: Where Did Trick-Or-Treating Come From?
summary: We aren’t exactly sure who invented trick-or-treating – kids who realized they could extort adults for candy, or adults who bought off kids in exchange for laying off pranks? The bigger question is: Will trick-or-treating survive the 21st century? Learn more in this classic episode.

title: Kindness: Do It
summary: In the tradition of our episodes on forgiveness and revenge, comes the third installment in the Emotional Roller Coaster trilogy. Kindness, it turns out, really does make the world go round.

title: Short Stuff: Candy Corn
summary: Is it vile? Is it delicious? It seems to be both! Hear all about the history of candy corn, how it’s made, and who likes it in this pre-Halloween episode!

title: The Criminal Father of Criminology
summary: Eugene Francois Vidocq is without a doubt one of the most interesting figures in modern history. He’s a former criminal turned undercover informant who went on to found the French national police force and the world’s first private detective agency.

title: Selects: Pain Scales: Yeeeow!
summary: Pain is subjective; it is whatever the person experiencing it says it is. But to effectively treat pain, it helps to quantify it, which is why medicine came up with pain scales. Learn all about them in this classic episode.

title: How Intellectual Property Works
summary: Intellectual property sounds as dry as can be, but it’s actually very interesting. It’s at the heart of the global economy and the center of a dispute over what should belong to the people who create things, from poetry to pharmaceuticals.

title: Short Stuff: Longyou Caves
summary: What’s better than discovering a mysterious cavern? Discovering five!

title: Parasocial Relationships: That Podcaster is Your Friend!
summary: Parasocial relationships are fascinating and it turns out Chuck knows what it's like from both sides. Listen in today to your old friends.

title: Selects: How Motion Sickness Works
summary: Motion sickness is the worst and hits about 25 to 40 percent of humans when they ride in cars, boats, or simply watch the wrong 3-D movie. Join us as we break down the science behind this nausea-inducing affliction in this classic episode.

title: How Andy Warhol Worked
summary: You know Andy Warhol from his quip on being famous for 15 minutes and paintings of soup cans, but even as far as artists go he was an eccentric and misunderstood person.

title: Short Stuff: Rhodium
summary: Rhodium is one of the most valuable precious metals on Earth, though it has dropped in value by about 80% in the last year. Learn why by clicking play.

title: Night of the Grizzlies
summary: Grizzly bears had never killed a person in Glacier National Park until the night of August 12, 1967. That's when everything changed for National Parks moving forward.

title: Selects: Social Security Numbers: Less Boring Than You'd Think
summary: Do you know that up until July 2011 an ambitious hacker with a good software program could deduce your social security number based on your date and place of birth? In this classic episode, the boys examine some of the lesser-known details of the Social Security system in the U.S.

title: Revenge: Bitter, Not Sweet
summary: Someone cuts you off in traffic or makes fun of your friend and all you can think of is how to get back at them and then some. But wait! Research has found that taking revenge actually makes you feel worse in the long run. Learn about what to do instead.

title: Short Stuff: The Dakota
summary: The Dakota is one of New York City's great buildings. And its backstory is pretty great to boot.

title: The Amazing Life of Christine Granville
summary: Christine Granville was about as James Bond as it gets. Stories of her life as a spy during World War II are legendary. Today we'll tell her story.

title: Selects: Cockney Rhyming Slang: Beautiful Gibberish
summary: What is Cockney Rhyming Slang? It's complicated and its origins are unclear. Learn everything we know about it today in this classic episode.

title: Kombucha: Fizzy Goodness
summary: Kombucha is pretty popular right now. But what is it exactly and where did it come from? The answers await you!

title: Short Stuff: Origin of Math Signs
summary: Have you ever stopped mid-pencil mark and realized to your astonishment where the plus sign came from? Then this one’s for you.

title: 10ish Worst Business Decisions Ever
summary: It’s easy (and kind of fun) to laugh at the misfortune of CEOs and other high up business types when they bring it on themselves – so let’s do that now. Herein lies some of the worst business decisions ever made, hindsight being 20/20, of course.

title: Selects: How Floods Work
summary: Floods happen when more water is introduced to an area than can be quickly removed. That's about it, but there's more to floods, what causes them and the havoc they can wreak. Join Josh and Chuck in this super-saturated classic episode of Stuff You Should Know.

title: The Hyatt Regency Skywalk Disaster
summary: In 1981 America suffered the worst accidental structural collapse in its history. Listen in today to the tragic story of the fast-tracked building disaster that stills haunts Kansas City.

title: Short Stuff: Why Spilling Salt is Unlucky
summary: Face it, when you spill salt your life goes totally off the rails, maybe even forever. Fortunately, we humans stumbled upon the one reliable way to counteract that bad luck by tossing some over our left shoulder.

title: Axolotls: The Smiling Salamander from Mexico
summary: It’s a listener request! Axolotls are one of the more amazing animals roaming the planet right now – they can regenerate parts of their brains, can fight off tumors, are found in the wild only in one single lake? And did we mention they smile all the time?

title: Selects: How Space Stations Work
summary: It seems like we largely take it for granted these days, but the fact that we have humans living in space is the realization of a scientific dream a century old. Visit the space stations orbiting Earth past, present and future in this classic episode.

title: Native American Reservations
summary: Today we dive into the history and current state of Native American reservations. This serves as a nice follow-up to the Trail of Tears double-ep from 2017.

title: Short Stuff: History of OK
summary: Is OK the best word? It's certainly one of the most versatile. Check the interesting history of this weird contraction.

title: The Made-up Disease of Syndrome K
summary: In WWII, Italy went through its own Jewish Holocaust, terrible at first then horrific as the Nazis took over the country. In Rome, a group of doctors hid Jewish refugees in plain sight in their hospital by giving them a highly contagious, highly fictitious disease.

title: Selects: Body Odor: You Stink
summary: Chuck and Josh end up making reduxes of past episodes on things like sweating and deodorant in this all-new episode on the science beneath what makes people smell. Learn all about your odor in this classic episode.

title: Laurens Hammond: The Non-Musical Genius Who Changed Popular Music
summary: Laurens Hammond invented the Hammond organ and in the process changed music history. But he was much more than that.

title: Short Stuff: Evil Eye
summary: You've seen the evil eye. Many Middle Eastern cultures have a long history with it. Learn how to thwart this curse today.

title: Fordlandia: Brazil Isn't Michigan
summary: Henry Ford tried to build a Midwestern American town in the Amazon rainforest in the 1920s. It's true. And yes, Chuck will say this should be a movie.

title: Selects: How Toy Testing Works
summary: It's every kid's dream - a job playing with toys that pays in toys. It's a real thing and has been around for a long time. Then there's the other side of the testing process, companies who ensure that toys are safe. It takes both of these testing techniques to successfully bring a toy to market these days. Dive into the ball pit with us today and learn all about toy testing in this classic episode.

title: Plant Migration
summary: Climate change is having sweeping effects on our climate and this is changing the world, not just for humans and other animals, but plants too. Will the Earth’s flora manage to find safe refuge in time?

title: Short Stuff: Saturn's Rings
summary: Friends, treasure Saturn’s rings while they are young. They won’t be around forever.

title: Farmer's Almanac: Literature to Poop To
summary: The Farmer's Almanac has a long rich history that is more than just moon phases and long-term weather patterns. Tune in to learn all about it.

title: Selects: How Music Sampling Works
summary: Today music sampling is a common practice, especially in electronic or hip-hop music. But how does it work? After all, other artists made the original music, and most of them would presumably like to be paid. Tune in to this classic episode to learn more about music sampling.

title: The Mysterious Disappearance of the Franklin Expedition
summary: One of the great Arctic mysteries was the disappearance of the ill-fated Franklin Expedition in search of a northwest passage between the Atlantic and Pacific. Not one man survived the trip, and they left precious little behind in the way of clues.

title: Short Stuff: Edward Mordake
summary: In the 19th century news spread of an unfortunate man who was born with an evil second face on the back of his head that spoke to him. The real story is that people keep falling for it.

title: How We’re Learning to Talk to Animals
summary: If we could talk with the animals, grunt and squeak and squawk with the animals, what would we say? We’d better start thinking of something good because researchers are learning to speak sperm whale, prairie dog, and a bunch of other species' languages.

title: Selects: How Magnets Work
summary: You can stick them to the fridge or use them to transpose sound to tape, whatever they are used for magnets are surprisingly interesting. And knowing just exactly how and why magnets work will make you more interesting, which is why you should listen to this classic episode of SYSK.

title: Xenobiotics
summary: Science is just realizing the extent of the tiny pollutants that have entered ecosystems across Earth and inside all humans. We call them xenobiotics – substances foreign to our bodies – and what effects they have on us we’re only starting to learn.

title: Short Stuff: History of English
summary: Who spoke English first and what was it like? Nothing like it is today. Listen in to learn all about it.

title: Dear Diary...
summary: Diaries have been around for a long time. There are many famous ones, and tens of millions that will never see the light of day. Learn about the history and benefits of journaling today.

title: Selects: Rainbows: Delighting humanity since forever
summary: Rainbows seem to defy nature, but they're really pretty simple when it comes down to it. Turns out it's just light reacting to water droplets in the air. But they sure do look cool. Learn all about how rainbows are formed in this classic episode.

title: The Last Meal Ritual
summary: The last meal of the executed is a longstanding tradition. Listen in today to learn about the dark history and modern practice of this culinary curiosity.

title: Short Stuff: NATO Alphabet
summary: Alpha, Bravo, Charlie. This is the NATO alphabet. But where did it come from?

title: BPD: The Worst Disorder or Not a Disorder at All?
summary: Borderline Personality Disorder has been described as emotional “third degree burns over ninety percent of your body.” It’s as close to a curse as a personality disorder can be: deep fear of being abandoned creates behaviors that end up driving people off.

title: Selects: What's the deal with Stradivarius violins?
summary: The Strad violin is noted for its tonal qualities and superior craftsmanship. And for its price tag. There are many theories why the Strad sounds so great, from the wood to the lacquer, to the simple fact that Antonio Stradivari was really good at what he did. Rosin up your bow and take a listen to this classic episode.

title: MAD Magazine: A Tribute
summary: Chuck and Josh grew up on MAD Magazine and we hope you did too. What started out as a comic book that spoofed comic books grew into the foundation of American satire and cultivated a healthy skepticism in generations of kids. Hail to the clods at MAD!

title: Short Stuff: Blue Highway Signs
summary: In the US those ubiquitous blue highway signs that tell you which direction you’ll find a Burger King have an interesting backstory.

title: Learning a Foreign Language
summary: Today, Chuck and Josh dive into the ins and outs of language learning.

title: Selects: Nirvana: Not The Band
summary: Hinduism and Buddhism are closely related in a number of ways, including their vision of what comes after we exit this mortal coil. Learn about the religions' interesting interpretation of the state of existence outside space-time, in this classic episode.

title: Magic Eye Illusions
summary: What became the Magic Eye illusion fad of the 1990s was born by way of the stereogram of the 1950s (and even before that). It's a winding story that you'll love!

title: Short Stuff: Pie-In-The-Face Gag
summary: Throwing a pie in someone’s face was groundbreaking comedy once upon a time.

title: Insomnia: Why you can't sleep
summary: Insomnia is rough stuff. Listen in and learn all about why you can't fall asleep and what you can do about that.

title: Selects: How Police Lineups Work
summary: Police lineups are something most people have never had any firsthand experience with. What you see on TV and in movies isn't so far off though. Learn about how these tropes work for real in this classic episode.

title: How PCP Works
summary: There is probably no drug more mythologized than PCP. It drives users insane and has the unfortunate side effect of bestowing superhuman strength thus sending them on a rampage. But does it though?

title: Short Stuff: Père-Lachaise Cemetery
summary: The most famous cemetery in Paris has some of the most famous people in the world buried there. And it's quite lovely.

title: Birth Order: So nice, we did it twice
summary: This is a very special episode, the first one we've ever fully recorded a second time and decided to release. Why? Because it's good and a little different and we thought you'd enjoy this unheard of double dose. So enjoy!

title: Selects: How Bats Work
summary: They are creepy, sure, but they are also useful, cute and in great danger of extinction. Get a new lease on life from a new view of bats in this classic episode.

title: James Beard: Food Legend
summary: James Beard is well-known now for the annual awards named in his honor. But he used to be the most famous chef in America, and set the standard for what makes a celebrity chef.

title: Short Stuff: Hollywood Sign
summary: The Hollywood sign is an iconic landmark that started out as a real estate billboard. Can you believe it?

title: How Trucking Works
summary: If truckers suddenly vanished the global economy would come to a grinding halt in a couple days. But as important as they are these highway heroes (mostly) are, they’re systematically mistreated by their industry.

title: Selects: What Makes Lead So Poisonous?
summary: The people of Flint, MI were horrified to find their drinking water was poisoned with lead. As we learn more about lead's effects and realize how persistent it is, the more worrying it becomes. What makes lead so toxic? Find out in this classic episode.

title: Butterflies: Caterpillars with Wings!
summary: If you thought caterpillars were awesome, just wait until you see them with colorful, iridescent wings!

title: Short Stuff: Fahrenheit or Celsius
summary: Fahrenheit or Celsius? Why not both? If they can agree - exactly at -40 degrees - then it seems like we should all be able to agree they're both great as well.

title: Caterpillars: Nature's Magicians
summary: Caterpillars are simply the best. Don't think so? Well listen in and you'll soon agree

title: Selects: How Ocean Currents Work
summary: It's easy to overlook the importance of ocean currents - they move along out at sea, while we stay mostly on land. But we are globally affected by them every day. Currents form the base of the food chain, drive weather and keep life as we know it going. Explore them with Josh and Chuck in this classic episode.

title: How Afrofuturism Works
summary: Black sci-fi writers were shut out of their genre in the 20th century so they created their own vision of the future. That sentiment spread to music and film and today it’s so engrained in pop culture it doesn't need its own label.

title: Short Stuff: Chia Pet
summary: It has arrived, the most important podcast episode in the history of the world.

title: Large Language Models and You
summary: There is a good chance that in March of 2023, humans crossed a threshold into a transformative new era when a new, smarter type of AI was let loose in the wild and an AI arms race began.

title: Selects: SYSK Live: Back When Ford Pintos Were Flaming Deathtraps
summary: For this special live benefit episode recorded in Atlanta, Josh and Chuck go back to the 70s and look at the decidedly ungroovy course of events that led to Ford recalling its Pinto after people started burning up in them.

title: How Alumin(i)um Works
summary: Humans made it through the Bronze Age and Iron Age, then we dabbled in steel, and now we are living in the Aluminum Age. The metal is so ubiquitous it seems like it’s been around forever, but we’ve only been really using it since the 20th century.

title: Short Stuff: Suicide Forest
summary: The suicide forest in Japan is a beautiful place with a checkered reputation. Trigger Warning: This episode features a discussion of suicide. If you or anyone you know needs help, please call 988.

title: The Stinky History of Human Hygiene
summary: Ever wondered when and why people started caring about body odors and cleanliness? Well look no further than today's episode.

title: Selects: How Audience Testing Works
summary: Did you know some of our most beloved movies originally had different, sometimes better, endings? That is until they were tested in front of focus groups. Learn all about the how, what, and why of audience testing in this classic episode.

title: Is Reality Real?
summary: Philosophers have been wondering whether we experience reality as it is for millennia now. They’ve pretty much settled on no, no we don’t. Now science has taken up the investigation and it’s proving the philosophers correct. So what is reality then?

title: Short Stuff: DNA Data Storage
summary: One of the more futuristic things around right now on Earth is research into encoding data into strings of genetic code.

title: Why Manners?
summary: Keeping your elbows off the table, keeping your fingers out of the gravy boat – at some point these became very important rules of etiquette. But what purpose do manners serve? It turns out they just may be the glue that prevents society from unraveling.

title: Selects: Pterosaurs: Not Flying Dinosaurs
summary: Almost everything you know about pterosaurs is wrong. They weren't birds, they weren't flying dinosaurs and they weren't all pterodactyls. Which makes this classic episode a great one for you to learn some new and amazing stuff about terrifying prehistoric beasts!

title: What's the deal with intermittent fasting?
summary: Could eating at only certain times of the day lead to weight loss? Possibly!

title: Short Stuff: Rube Goldberg
summary: Everyone knows what a Rube Goldberg machine is, but what do you know about the cartoonist who they're named after?

title: The Saga of Milli Vanilli
summary: For a moment Milli Vanilli was the hottest musical act in the world. Then came the news that it was just that, an act, and the fall came swiftly and humiliatingly. Now, 30 years on, a look back yields not so much a cautionary tale as a very sad story.

title: Selects: How Color Works
summary: Science doesn't have a good explanation for why we sense color, yet it is everywhere and affecting us all the time. But why should minutely different wavelengths of light have such an impact on our moods and motivations? Explore these questions and more with Josh and Chuck in this classic episode.

title: The Semi-Recent History of Exercise
summary: Humans exercising for better health has not been around that long. Today we dive into this fun history as we cover why and when we started this now commonplace pastime.

title: Short Stuff: Pollen Count
summary: If you watch the news and hear the pollen count is high for some particular type of plant then it’s high time you learned how they do that.

title: What is the Bechdel Test?
summary: The Bechdel Test is a is a measure of the representation of women in film. You'd be surprised how many movies fail.

title: Selects: How Dog Shows Work
summary: You know those shows where people wearing sensible shoes jog dogs around in circles? They actually represent the pinnacle of a long and complex path to glory for dogs and their owners. Join Chuck and Josh as they peek inside the American dog show in this classic episode.

title: How Juries Work
summary: It’s totally bonkers that in the US and other countries, the job of determining the guilt or innocence of an accused criminal – whose life may be at stake – is left not to experts in law but to a group of random citizens. Even crazier, it generally works!

title: Short Stuff: Mood Rings
summary: Mood Rings were all the rage in the 1970s. Then they went away, and fast. What's your color today?

title: The Inflammation Theory of Disease
summary: Not too long ago we thought that germs were the cause of most diseases, leading to germ theory. But when we look at maladies from heart disease to Alzheimer’s one commonality stands out: inflammation. Could it be we’ve found the root cause of all diseases?

title: Selects: How Slinky Works
summary: It has been called a "glorified spring", but Slinky is one of the best selling toys of all time. From accidental origins to an unlikely resurrection, Slinky has a pretty great back story. Learn all about it in this classic episode.

title: How TV Weathercasters Work
summary: TV weather people can seem corny and maybe a little nerdy, but beneath that toothsome exterior lies the heart of a lonely warrior of science, one who is often overlooked as the hardest working member of the news team. Learn all about these unsung heroes.

title: Short Stuff: Frances Kelsey: Hero of the FDA
summary: Who is Frances Kelsey? Well, she's a semi-unsung hero of the FDA whose work helped save a lot of kids from congenital disorders and even death. Listen and learn!

title: The Colosseum
summary: It's funny how similar The Colosseum in Rome is to modern day arenas. They really had it figured out. Tune in today to learn all about this early entertainment venue.

title: Selects: Does the body replace itself?
summary: Does the human body really replace itself every few years? The answer is yes, but different parts of the body do so at different rates. Learn all about which parts of your body are the speediest, and which take the longest to regenerate, in this classic episode.

title: Introducing Smell-O-Vision!
summary: Smell-O-Vision was a post-war movie theater gimmick that delivered well-timed scents to the noses of audiences to align with the movie. Did it work? Sort of. Did it ultimately fail? Yes. Does that mean it has gone away forever? No.

title: Short Stuff: Dunbar's Number
summary: There’s a theory that all of us have a maximum number of friendships that we can maintain – 150, to be exact. Suspiciously exact, really, if you think about it.

title: Nerf!
summary: Another classic toys edition is at your collective feet. Today, we dive into the soft, padded world of NERF!

title: Selects: How Manhunts Work
summary: When a suspect or prisoner goes on the lam there are plenty of ways to hide: in plain sight, in the mountains, in another country. There are as many types of ways law enforcement uses to track wanted people as their are ways to go on the lam, but there are some founding principles to carrying out a successful manhunt and they actually include you. Learn about how the fuzz tracks down fugitives and how it's evolving in the age of social media in this classic episode.

title: Carbon Monoxide: Please Just Listen Anyway
summary: It might not be the sexiest topic we’ve ever covered (and by “might”, we mean “definitely”), but there are some things you just need to learn about and this deadly and undetectable gas that’s part of our everyday lives is one of them. So buck up.

title: Short Stuff: Botox Brain
summary: Botox can chase away the lines on your face, apparently it can chase away your depression, borderline personality disorder, and anxiety too.

title: Why does everyone love Dolly Parton?
summary: Today we dive in to celebrate the international treasure that is Dolly Parton. Why is she nearly universally loved? Listen in to find out.

title: Selects: Was There A Real Robin Hood?
summary: Is it true that Robin Hood hung out in Sherwood Forest and stole from the rich to give to the poor? No. No, it’s not. Find out the real story in this classic episode.

title: METI: Existential Threat? Probably Yes
summary: We've wanted to contact extraterrestrials for as long as we've suspected they're out there. But as we get better and locating potentially inhabited planets, beaming messages their way is suddenly posing a threat.

title: Short Stuff: Routines
summary: Routines are a key part of a successful life. Ask anybody about theirs and they'll be happy to share!

title: Should Rich Countries Cancel Poor Countries’ Debt?
summary: It sounds controversial, but there are persuasive arguments for the wealthy Global North to write off the debts lower-income nations have accrued. Some say the US and Europe actually owe it to them. This is one of those boring ones you shouldn’t skip.

title: Selects: How Coffins Work
summary: Sure, you've probably laid in one at the store or a funeral home, but how much do you know about receptacles used to bury the dead? We'll bet you'll learn plenty - like the difference between a coffin and a casket - in this classic episode.

title: John Brinkley: The Quackiest Quack in History?
summary: John Brinkley was perhaps the biggest quack who ever claimed to be practicing medicine. Learn all about this not so good guy today!

title: Short Stuff: Red Snow
summary: Thanks to green algae, there's such a thing as red snow. And we've recently found it can accelerate global warming. Look out!

title: How Skydiving Works
summary: At 13,000 feet the ground is nothing but far-away squares of land, and you can even see some clouds below you. All of a sudden you find yourself plummeting downward. There are very few thrills like jumping out of a plane with a parachute.

title: Selects: Some Nutso Fan Theories
summary: It turns out that the characters in your favorite TV shows and the like are actually dead, dreaming, dying or don't exist. Explore some strange fan theories with Josh and Chuck in this classic episode.

title: Playing Cards? You Got That Right!
summary: If you've ever wanted to learn more about playing cards, now is your big chance.

title: Short Stuff: Beethoven’s DNA
summary: It's been all over the news, Beethoven's DNA has revealed some interesting things about his health.

title: What Caused the Late Bronze Age Collapse?
summary: Humans’ first attempt at civilization went pretty well for the first thousand years. Important stuff like the wheel, writing, math, art, and diplomacy came out of it. But then, in the blink of an historical eye, it all mysteriously failed. What happened?

title: Selects: How Jet Lag Works
summary: It was only since 1958 that the Jet Age began, and jet lag became a real condition. Also known as desynchronosis, jet lag can lead to all manner of ailments, from sleeplessness to irritability to diabetes and cancer. In this classic episode, learn about how the body's natural clock runs normally and what happens when it gets out of whack when we cross time zones quickly.

title: What's the deal with dowsing?
summary: Dowsing, aka water-witching has been around a long time. And you might be surprised that's still a thing. We get into all the nitty gritty of this pseudo-science today.

title: Short Stuff: Theme Park Cremations
summary: There’s a little-discussed trend you might run into at your favorite theme park – people scattering the ashes of a loved one on rides. Here's hoping you don't literally run into it.

title: The First Road Trip
summary: Back when cars were a brand new thing, before people even knew they'd stick around, two men and a dog drove from San Francisco to New York. This is their story.

title: Selects: Is The Uncanny Valley Real?
summary: In 1970, roboticist Masahiro Mori wrote an essay that said the closer robots come to lifelike, the more they unsettle humans. His theory became the Uncanny Valley, and science has been evaluating it – and what makes something creepy - in recent years. Learn all about it with Josh and Chuck in this classic episode.

title: An Interesting, Vastly Incomplete Look at Baseball Cards
summary: One of the all-stars of the hobby world is collecting baseball cards. Over time it’s gone from a kids’ hobby to a major investment vehicle, complete with its own bubble that recently burst. But at the heart of it is something both engrossing and endearing.

title: Short Stuff: Semantic Satiation
summary: You know when you read a word over and over it starts to lose its meaning? There’s a term for that and why it happens is fascinating.

title: The Tragic Tale of Floyd Collins
summary: Floyd Collins was a natural-born caver who met a terrible fate, becoming stuck underground where no one could get him loose. His unlucky, slowly unfolding plight also turned out to be one of the first national media sensations of the 20th century.

title: Selects: Do People Really Run Off to Join the French Foreign Legion?
summary: Anyone who knows anything about Jean-Claude Van Damme knows he played a French legionnaire in the movies. He was just one of many actors to star in films that romanticized this mercenary force. Check out the details in this classic episode with Josh and Chuck.

title: Arcades: Nostalgia Abounds
summary: Chuck and Josh were around during the Golden Age of the arcade. And look how they turned out! Join them on a trip down memory lane.

title: Short Stuff: John Cage's 639 Year Concert
summary: John Cage was a unique artist to say the least. Learn all about this avant-garde composer today.

title: That's Amaro!
summary: Amaro is a delicious traditional liqueur, usually from Italy, that has delighted diners and drinkers for centuries. Tune in to learn all about this wonderful digestif.

title: Selects: The Time Nazis Invaded Florida
summary: During World War II, Nazis invaded the United States with saboteurs bent on fomenting chaos. Three times. Learn all about it in this classic episode.

title: Woodstock: The Festival for Stardust, Golden Hippies
summary: You may have heard your parents or – gasp – grandparents prattle on about how amazing the original 1969 Woodstock Festival was. It turns out that, as much as people who lived through the 60s like to talk them up, Woodstock really was that amazing.

title: Short Stuff: Paprika
summary: Paprika is more than a smoky Hungarian spice. Actually, that's not true, that's exactly what it is. But it sure is delicious!

title: Noncompete Agreements, Come On
summary: A noncompete agreement, a pledge not to work for a competitor for a set amount of time, makes sense – when the worker is well compensated and privy to company secrets. But that doesn’t describe the vast majority of workers who’ve signed noncompetes.

title: Selects: Live From San Francisco: How Malls Work
summary: In this classic show recorded live on January 5, 2017 at San Francisco’s Castro Theatre, Josh and Chuck delve into the history and the heyday of the church of consumerism and what it means for local communities and our capitalist society at large when malls die.

title: Crosswords episode, perhaps?
summary: Crossword puzzles have an interesting history and are a lot of fun to do. Dive in today to learn about Chuck's latest obsession.

title: Short Stuff: La Pascualita
summary: In a bridal shop in Chihuahua, Mexico a mannequin has been standing in the window since the 1930s that’s so lifelike some say it’s actually a corpse.

title: The Awe-Inspiring, Absolutely Crucial Amazon
summary: If you’ve ever thought, “What’s the Amazon rainforest ever done for me? Nothin, that’s what,” then you’re dead wrong, friend. It covers 1 percent of the Earth’s surface but houses perhaps 30 percent of its species and it’s invaluable to all life on Earth.

title: Selects: Who Committed the 1912 Villisca Ax Murders?
summary: In a small town in Iowa in 1912 eight people were murdered in the grisliest of ways while they slept. Local reputations were ruined when accusations flew, but could a drifting serial killer working across the Midwest have been behind it? Learn all about it with Josh and Chuck in this classic episode.

title: Naps: Chuck's Secret Talent
summary: Naps are great if you can manage to find the space to take them. The trick is to do it for the right amount of time. We get into all in the ins and outs of Chuck's favorite time of day.

title: Short Stuff: Sleeping On It
summary: It’s pretty well known that if you wait to make a big decision until after you get some sleep, you’re likelier to make a good one. But why should that be? Why, we’ll explain if only you’d listen.

title: The Mystery of the Lost Amber Room
summary: Chuck and Josh turn into the Hardy Boys for one of the great unsolved mysteries of WWII, a work of art worth a king’s ransom that went missing in 1945.

title: Selects: The Max Headroom Affair
summary: In 1987, a very strange broadcast intrusion occurred in the city of Chicago. For just a couple of minutes, the odd TV character Max Headroom appeared onscreen in the middle of an episode of Dr. Who. He spoke in garbled tones, brandished a marital aid, and was spanked on the rear with a fly swatter by a person dressed in Annie Oakley garb. If this sounds weird, it is. It's the Max Headroom Incident. Find out all about it in this classic episode.

title: The Beverly Hills Supper Club Fire
summary: The fire at the Beverly Hills Supper Club was not in Los Angeles, but Kentucky. Which happened to be Las Vegas before Vegas was Vegas. Confused? Listen in and all will be clear.

title: Short Stuff: Beulah Mae Donald
summary: In 1981 a Mobile mother of six was forced into the role of civil rights activist when the Klan murdered her son and she was moved to fight back.

title: The Glorious Flamingo
summary: Flamingos are much more than just pretty pink birds. They are in fact, quite remarkable! Listen and learn…

title: Selects: Cave Diving: Totally Nuts
summary: There are extreme sports and then there is cave diving, the most extreme activity a person can engage in without leaving Earth. Cave divers stay underwater swimming miles into – that’s right – caves, where no human has ever been before. It’s pretty cool. Wade in with Josh and Chuck in this classic episode.

title: How (O)possums Work
summary: Josh and Chuck take a listener’s suggestion – many, many suggestions – and learn that possums are pretty great and very much misunderstood. By the end of this episode you will too!

title: Short Stuff: No Shirt, No Shoes, WTF
summary: You can thank your parents and grandparents for the longstanding ban against dining shirtless and shoeless. While the concept was around, it mushroomed when hippies came along.

title: Honey: Nature's Wonder Sugar
summary: Honey is an amazing thing. Just ask any bee. They make a ton of it. So much that humans get what bees can't use and that's a lot of honey.

title: Selects: How Easy Bake Ovens Work
summary: Easy Bake Ovens are as iconic as a toy can get, as American as apple pie or baseball. Learn all about these light bulb cooking, working ovens that endanger children to this day, in this classic episode.

title: The Largely Equine History of Veterinary Medicine
summary: Vets have been around for a long time, but mainly to care for horses. When horse travel went away, guess who saved the profession? Dogs!

title: Short Stuff: Bird Migration
summary: Where are all those birds flying anyway? How do they decide? When do they do it? All of these questions, and more, are answered in this week's ep.

title: Must We Suffer Emotional Pain?
summary: It’s part of the human condition, to feel the pain of sorrow, loss, embarrassment. But isn’t it kind of weird that an overwhelming emotion can cause you physical discomfort or even pain? Turns out that depends on how you think about the mind and the body.

title: Selects: Elephants: The Best Animals?
summary: Elephants are pretty much the best. Why? Josh and Chuck will let you know in great detail in this classic episode.

title: How Attachment Theory Works
summary: A theory in the field of psychology has become so pervasive, it’s generally taken on faith that it’s true. It says that how your parents respond to you during a short window in your infancy has lifelong effects on your personality. Could this be correct?

title: Short Stuff: Adam's Apples and Throat Lumps
summary: This week's short stuff is all about throat lumps and Adam's apples.

title: Let's Talk About John DeLorean
summary: John DeLorean: visionary, car maker extraordinaire, buyer of large amounts of cocaine, provider of time machine chassis. There is a lot to understand about John DeLorean so let’s get busy.

title: Selects: How Game Shows Work
summary: Join Josh and Chuck and a whole bunch of great people at the Gothic Theatre in Denver for this live show on game shows and their place in cultures around the world, recorded on June 28, 2018. You just come right on down, why don’t you?

title: Toast: As in browned bread
summary: Toast is bread that has been browned by heat. It's delicious. This is our ode to toast.

title: Short Stuff: Women Pirates
summary: The Golden Age of Pirates didn’t have just men floating on the high seas. Some women became very successful pirates and today you’ll learn about two of them.

title: The Louisiana Purchase: Not a Purchase
summary: Turns out the Louisiana Purchase was not so much a purchase, but the right to (steal) purchase it from indigenous peoples. But it did transform the United States as we know it. Listen and learn!

title: Selects: How Therapeutic Hypothermia Works
summary: Physicians noticed centuries ago that people exposed to cold temperatures often have amazing recoveries from serious medical emergencies. Now medicine is learning how to purposefully induce hypothermia in order to buy time to fix otherwise fatal trauma. Find out all about it in this classic episode.

title: How Tarot Works?
summary: This is not a hit piece! Tarot helps plenty of people navigate their lives and reflect on their feelings – plus the art is unbelievable. We cover the backstory, real and imagined, and lure the innocent into tarot’s grip, er, offer basic tips for beginners.

title: Short Stuff: Forest Lawn Memorial Park
summary: Forest Lawn is no ordinary cemetery. Why? Listen in and find out.

title: How Enron Fooled the World
summary: Until 2007, the largest single corporate bankruptcy was Enron, a $67 billion energy trading company. Its decline was breathtaking, and while it’s a fascinating story of corporate malfeasance and greed, it’s also about the lives of ruined workers.

title: Selects: How Perfume Works
summary: Women consistently rate scent as the most important factor in a man's attractiveness and men have been manipulating that for centuries with scents of all sorts. Learn about the fascinating history -- and, well, art -- of making perfumes in this classic episode.

title: When Mount St. Helens Blew Its Top
summary: Mount St. Helen's is a lovely sight to behold, but was a pretty scary thing to be around in the Spring of 1980. Listen in to the harrowing story today!

title: Short Stuff: Dangers of Nose Picking
summary: You don’t have to lie - everybody picks their nose. But did you know it can be life-threatening? It’s true and you can learn how in this episode.

title: The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald (not the song)
summary: Today Josh and Chuck delve into the wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald. Not the song, but the maritime accident. Though the song makes an appearance.

title: Selects: Could There Be A Loch Ness Monster?
summary: People have believed something strange lives in Loch Ness for at least 3500 years. Thousands of people have sighted the Loch Ness Monster and dozens of expeditions have been launched. But does the fact that nothing’s been found mean it’s not real? Find out in this classic episode.

title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show Podcast Episode
summary: This one goes out to the SYSK Army as a special request. Let's do the time warp again!

title: Short Stuff: Mesas: Flat
summary: Mesas, buttes and plateaus are all very similar. We'll break down the differences in each one just to be sure.

title: Juicy: The Fried Chicken Story
summary: Fried chicken is Chuck’s favorite food, and Josh sure doesn’t dislike it. It is with this appreciation that SYSK plunges into the hot grease of fried chicken history – and there’s a lot to it!

title: Selects: Star Wars Holiday Spectacular
summary: Long ago, in a galaxy not so far away, George Lucas allowed the Star Wars Holiday Special to be made. What happened on the night of November 17, 1978 can never be fully explained, but we make our best effort in our annual special edition of SYSK. May the force be with us all.

title: 2022 Holiday Spectacular!
summary: Another year comes to a close here at SYSK, which means our annual Holiday Spectacular is at hand. So light a fire, pour up a comforting beverage and gather the family for some good cheer!

title: Who was Dorothy Parker, really?
summary: She was known for her quick wit and sharp tongue. But she was also a poet, screenwriter and activist. Tune in today to learn what outside her "vicious circle."

title: Selects: Nostradamus: Predictor of the future? Not so much.
summary: Nostradamus delighted us all in grade school, but it turns out the real guy wasn't quite as prescient as we were led to believe. In truth, he wrote a lot of purposefully confusing riddles that people have twisted into meaning exactly what they want them to mean. Learn all about Nostradamus in this classic episode.

title: Interesting Origins of Everyday Phrases
summary: We don’t think about the words and phrases we use all the time - until Josh and Chuck look into them and tell everyone what they found. That’s the gist of this episode!

title: Short Stuff: The Atlanta Washer Woman Strike
summary: One of the very first union strikes in US history was mounted by a group of African American women in the deep South. Listen in and learn all about this little known slice of history.

title: How the Nintendo Entertainment System Changed Gaming Forever
summary: For the holidays in 1986 (and ’87) (and ’88) the most stupendous, most wanted, most amazing thing any kid could possibly get – outside of a pony, *maybe* – was the NES. That year, video games came back from the dead and changed forever.

title: Selects: How Polar Bears Work
summary: Polar bears are more than just lovable creatures that roam the ice in search of food. They're one of the most fascinating animals on planet Earth. Sadly, as ice shrinks, so does their habitat. Learn all about these huggable beasts in this classic episode.

title: True Crime: The Phantom of Heilbronn
summary: After the murder of a cop in southwest Germany in 2007 a massive hunt was launched across Europe. The suspect was a female serial killer who had left DNA behind during a number of crimes. She was so slippery, she was known as The Phantom of Heilbronn.

title: Short Stuff: Birthday Paradox
summary: The Birthday Paradox involves math, so you know this one will go perfectly.

title: How Face Blindness Works
summary: It’s not that the person who can never remember meeting you is snobby or even absent-minded; they may have a fascinating – and often difficult – neurological condition called prosopagnosia, known more commonly as face blindness.

title: Selects: The Rubik's Cube Episode
summary: Rubik's Cubes. Ronald Reagan. Jerry Falwell. Just Say No. One of these things was awesome. Take a guess and hop on board this classic episode, aka the 80s train.

title: How Down Syndrome Works
summary: People with Down syndrome lead rich, complex lives like any other human, but it’s only been in the last few decades that everyone else stopped persecuting them long enough to notice this. As a result, both their IQ and their life expectancy skyrocketed.

title: Short Stuff: Goosebumps
summary: Goosebumps are a pretty cool evolutionary holdover from our earlier days as furry beasts. Don't believe us? Listen in.

title: Peripersonal Space: Humans’ Got Talent
summary: The space around you that you can reach with your arms is a very special place. It’s where we interact with reality. And although we are so good at using it we don’t give it a second thought, our ability to use it is one our most amazing abilities.

title: Selects: How Umami Works!
summary: For millennia humans have recognized four tastes, but in the 1980s a fifth taste first isolated in Japan gained worldwide acceptance - and took off like a rocket! Learn about meaty, musty, savory umami in this classic episode.

title: Roller Skating: Fun and Cool
summary: The Victorians were the first to go bonkers for roller skating and since then the pastime has had bursts of popularity every few decades. Over the years skaters have come up with some amazing things to do on skates that go way beyond just going in circles.

title: Short Stuff: Liquid Paper
summary: Correction fluid goes by many names, but the OG was Liquid Paper. And it has a pretty cool origin story.

title: Typewriters: Mechanical Brilliance
summary: Chuck loves typewriters because he loves mechanical brilliance. Dive into the cool history of these amazing machines today.

title: Selects: How Dark Money Works
summary: Since the Supreme Court ruled in 2010 in the Citizens United case that political contributions are speech and should be protected, the floodgates of anonymous political contributions have opened. But does absolute funding corrupt absolutely? Find out in this classic episode.

title: Did Shakespeare really write all that stuff?
summary: The question of Shakespeare's authorship has been around since at least the mid-1800s. Is there anything to it? We'll dig in to this dense topic to find out.

title: Short Stuff: Incomplete Yawns
summary: Is there anything – anything – worse than a yawn you can’t finish? It’s hard to think of anything else and as your obsession with yawning like a normal human being grows it only becomes more difficult. Why? Why?!

title: The Sordid History of Bachelor/Bachelorette Parties
summary: When it comes to pre-wedding festivities, bachelor and bachelorette parties take the penis-shaped cake. Learn all about these sordid affairs today.

title: Selects: Finders Keepers: Real Law
summary: You know that heartbreak of the schoolyard – finders keepers, losers weepers? That’s actual law in a great many grown up places. Enter the murky legal world of finding something that belongs to someone else, from buried treasure to a misplaced ring. Learn all about it in this classic episode.

title: How Owls Work
summary: It’s time for another great animal episode and in this one we swoop into the world of owls – nature’s greatest silent predator who (hooo) also look very cute and intelligent. Not to mention they can turn their heads 270 degrees.

title: Short Stuff: Dodleston Messages
summary: It’s not everyday that a message from the 16th century appears on a computer from the 1980s, so when that happened it caught an English couple’s attention and launched a still-unresolved mystery - across tiiiiiiime!

title: What's so important about legal precedent?
summary: Legal precedent is an odd thing. It matters, but it isn't codified. There are advantages and disadvantages. Let's all dive in and take at STARE DECISIS today.

title: Selects: What is an invasive species?
summary: Invasive species can mean a lot of things, from fungus to feral pigs and European starlings to kudzu vines. Basically, it's anything brought to a place, either by humans or nature, that didn't originate there. They aren't always a problem, but many times they can wreak havoc on the local ecosystem. Learn all about these invaders in this classic episode.

title: Vaudeville: Step Right Up!
summary: In today's episode, you will learn everything you ever wanted to know about vaudeville, whether you like it or not.

title: Short Stuff: Birth Certificate Access
summary: It’s unjust but true – if you are an adoptee in the US you may not have the same right to access your birth certificate that someone who wasn’t adopted does. The quest to access a birth certificate can be a legal rigamarole that may or may not work.

title: The Harvey's Casino Bombing of 1980
summary: In August of 1980 a bomb containing 1,000 pounds of dynamite was quietly delivered to Harvey’s, a casino and resort at Lake Tahoe. This kicked off a whirlwind caper that lasted 30 hours and ended up nearly demolishing the 11-story resort.

title: Selects: How Vampires Work
summary: Out of obligation, Chuck and Josh mention Twilight, but it is the longstanding vampire lore that gets the most attention in this examination of how the bloodsucking undead evolved from baby-stealing demonesses to suave counts in our collective psyche. Explore the wild world of vampires in this spooky classic episode.

title: The 13th Annual Halloween Spooktacular!
summary: It's hard to believe, but this is our 13th edition of the Halloween Spooktacular! So pour up a creepy brew and gather the kids for a dramatic reading of two horror shorts.

title: Short Stuff: Robert the Doll
summary: Robert the Doll is decidedly creepy. So is his story. Listen in to this spooky tale right now!

title: The Tale of the Bloody Benders
summary: Long before we knew what serial killers were, a family in remote Kansas was disposing of victims at their family farm. Listen in to the Tale of the Bloody Benders if you dare!

title: Selects: 10ish Cases of Really Bad Luck
summary: Some guys have all the luck, some guys have all the pain. So said Rod Stewart. And if this list is any indication, “guys” is gender neutral. Listen to this classic episode as Chuck and Josh cover some instances of amazingly bad fortune, most of it true!

title: Fundamentalism: Menace II Society
summary: Fundamentalism is usually thought of as a problem religions have to deal with, but not all fundamentalists are religious. And no matter what their belief system, fundamentalism is inherently antisocial and a problem for everyone.

title: Short Stuff: Water Towers
summary: Water towers are so ubiquitous you can look right past them, despite them being giant balls of water thrust triumphantly skyward. Learn about these surprisingly ingenious but simple inventions designed to keep you alive.

title: The History of Fake Towns.
summary: There have been a lot of fake towns built throughout history for a lot of different reasons. Tune in to learn about some of these bogus burgs.

title: Selects: How Pompeii Worked
summary: What must be one of the most famous natural disasters in history took place when Mt Vesuvius buried Pompeii in 79 CE. But when the town was resurrected 1700 years later, a new chapter in its history was written. Learn all about it in this classic episode.

title: 10 Cases of Mistaken Identity
summary: There’s a lot that can go wrong when your identity is at question. Charged with abandoning a baby? Check. Years in prison? That too. Accused of assassinating the head of Hamas? Why not. Learn about the travails of some unlucky saps in this episode.

title: Short Stuff: Blaschko's Lines
summary: Did you know you have stripes? It’s true, you just can’t see them. Learn all about these little-known lines today!

title: Doppelgängers: Hey you, you're me!
summary: Seeing your near twin is probably pretty weird. But could there be a genetic commonality as well? You bet there could!

title: Selects: Josh and Chuck's List of Horror Movies that Changed the Genre
